item.title: About Me - Allen Nguyen
item.dc:creator: allenacnguyen
item.content:encoded:
Hi, my name is Allen Nguyen, and I am 25 years old, a multimedia designer, and a creator from Houston, TX.

Full Name: Allen-Tri Hai Nguyen
Born: July 28, 2000, Houston, Texas, United States

I was born as a first child to the Vietnamese family. Currently, I have a younger sister named Mindy and a younger brother named Henry, so I am the oldest child in my family.

I am a large fan of My Little Pony since 2013 that my sister first watched that TV show.

I have a YouTube channel since February 2013 and started uploading content since January 2014. I currently have around 18,000 subscribers with My Little Pony content at first. I would like for you to subscribe to my YouTube channel as it would help in the future for more content. I'm a monetized YouTuber since March 2025, after being demonetized in March 2019 for reused content. I'm a YouTuber that sometimes upload pony content, often congratulate big YouTubers (MrBeast, PewDiePie, Dream, BLACKPINK, Mark Rober, etc.) that surpassed such major milestones (20 million subscribers, 30 million, 50 million, 100 million, etc.) on the platform, often do news about events, and sometimes upload something miscellaneously.

My goal on YouTube is to reach 100,000 subscribers for the first time as I hope to be one of the most important creators for everyone. I also want to be famous too.

I started playing the piano at the age of 5, and the cello at the age of 10. I played both of those instruments for at least 10 years. I love hearing and playing music all the time. I also compose and arrange music too. I'm also a DJ too since my senior year in high school, and you can call me "DJ Blue" for that.

I am a graduate from the University of Houston holding a Bachelor of Science in Digital Media degree since May 2025 with Summa Cum Laude honors. My goal after graduation would be to continue to grow my YouTube channel, showcase my portfolio, and amending the United States Constitution helping the society in governmental reforms. I have particular interest in going for a Ph.D. degree that I would like everyone to call me Dr. Allen or Dr. Nguyen.

For channels that surpassed 50 million subscribers, I hope someone fills in to design a 50 Million Subscriber Custom Play Button. Daniel Krafft of course! My potential 50 Million Subscriber Custom Play Button design would be Twilight Sparkle from My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic with open wings.

Favorite Hobbies

  • Content Creator
  • Graphic Design
    • Adobe Photoshop
    • Adobe Illustrator
    • Adobe InDesign
  • Video Producer
    • Adobe Premiere Pro
    • Adobe After Effects (visual effects)
  • Professional Gamer
    • My Little Pony Gameloft
    • Minecraft
    • Microsoft Flight Simulator X
    • Prepar3D v4 (sometimes)
    • Some first-person shooter games (FPS)
    • Grand Theft Auto
  • Disc Jockey (DJ)
    • For any event that has a DJ booth, I want to be a DJ for the event too!
    • I also want to remix music of my favorite celebrity songs that has similar riffs.
  • Music Performance
    • Cello
    • Piano
    • Enthusiasm in musical instruments including some emphasis in brass and percussion
  • Music Conducting
    • Whenever the music is being played or performed, I want to conduct by waving my hands!
  • Music Composition & Arrangement
    • I'm willing to compose my first symphony.
    • Based on what I learned from theory, I want to be a good composer too inspired by classical composers (Beethoven, Mozart, Bach, etc.) and romantic composers (Chopin, Tchaikovsky, Schubert, Brahms, Rachmaninoff, etc.).
  • Bus Spotter
    • Groome Transportation of Texas, LLC; shuttle buses for Cougar Line including the Sugar Land route
  • Baseball
    • I want to play baseball too as both a pitcher and batter like Shohei Ohtani (who is a two-way player and was twice-unanimous American League Most Valuable Player in both 2021 and 2023 seasons). I will throw and bat right-handed while Ohtani bats left-handed.
    • A fan of the Houston Astros and so does the New York Yankees and Los Angeles Dodgers.
    • I want to visit the ballpark of Astros home games too!
  • Football
    • I also watch the Super Bowl, even I'm a Houston Texans fan.
    • I hope the Texans reach the AFC Championship Round for the first time in franchise history, and so does the Super Bowl.

PROFESSIONAL CAREER

  • Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra (2020 – present)
    • I started playing with this orchestra since February 2020 if I want to continue playing in the orchestra after I graduated from high school. My mother recommended me to play with this orchestra.

item.title: Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra: 2020–2021: Season 29
item.dc:creator: allenacnguyen
item.content:encoded:
These are the list of concerts performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra for the 2020–2021 season, the 29th season. There were four concerts performed for this season due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic in the Houston area in terms of social distancing and mask regulations.

This season was the last season Mr. Gregory McDaniel conducted with the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra as an Assistant Conductor before he pursued his master's degree at the University of North Texas.

Music Director and Conductor: Dr. Dominique Royem, D.M.A.
Assistant Conductor: Mr. Gregory McDaniel
Chorus Director: Mr. Adam J. Hightower-Moreno
Concertmistress: Aimee Petersen, violin

Fall 2020 Virtual Concert: Sunday, September 27, 2020 (virtual)
Deck the Halls 2020: December 2020 (virtual)
Our Hearts Are Whole Again!: Friday, August 6, 2021 (virtual)
Freedom Rings 2021: Sunday, July 4, 2021

Freedom Rings 2021

Sunday, July 4, 2021
[7:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

Freedom Rings is an annual 4th of July (Independence Day) concert performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra. It was performed on July 4th at the Stafford Centre every year regardless of weekday. The Freedom Rings Concert is free for everyone, so people who are invited to this concert are welcome.

There was no one-time intermission in this concert, because the City of Stafford does not want an intermission for the 4th of July Concert.

Our Hearts Are Whole Again!

Premiered on Friday, August 6, 2021 on Vimeo
[Virtual Concert @ Stafford Centre]

The concert was held virtually and digitally inside the Stafford Centre auditorium. No guests were invited during the recording session. It was held on Saturday, May 22, 2021 and the virtual concert was premiered on Friday, August 6, 2021 on Vimeo. This concert is also known as the Summer Virtual Concert. Additionally, no concerto pieces were performed for this concert since they don't have concerto winners in 2021 yet.

NOTE: The virtual concert video on Vimeo is private. You will have to contact the author of this post Allen Nguyen, a cello player and member of the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra, via private message to give you the password to access this virtual concert video. The video will not be shared or publicized without permission from the Music Director and Conductor of the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra, Dr. Dominique Royem, as it is due to copyright.

Deck the Halls 2020

Premiered on December 2020 on Vimeo
[Virtual Concert @ Christ Church Sugar Land Sanctuary]

The Deck the Halls concert is an annual Christmas and holiday concert hosted by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra. No concerto pieces were performed for this concert, as there were no concerto winners to play for this concert.

Due to COVID-19 pandemic in terms of social distancing and mask mandate regulations in order to reduce the chance of virus spread, the concert was held virtually and digitally inside the sanctuary at Christ Church Sugar Land. No guests were invited during the recording session.

NOTE: The virtual concert video on Vimeo is private. You will have to contact the author of this post Allen Nguyen, a cello player and member of the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra, via private message to give you the password to access this virtual concert video. The video will not be shared or publicized without permission from the Music Director and Conductor of the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra, Dr. Dominique Royem, as it is due to copyright.

Fall 2020 Virtual Concert

Sunday, September 27, 2020
[Virtual Concert]

Due to COVID-19 pandemic in terms of social distancing and mask mandates in order to reduce the chance of virus spread, the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra fall 2020 concert was virtual. No Hauntcert happened due to the pandemic as well.

item.title: Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra: 2021–2022: Season 30 (30th Anniversary)
item.dc:creator: allenacnguyen
item.content:encoded:
These are the list of concerts performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra for the 2021–2022 season, the 30th season. This was the 30th anniversary season of this orchestra. There were six concerts performed for this season.

Music Director and Conductor: Dr. Dominique Royem, D.M.A.
Assistant Conductor: Mr. William "Bill" Tackett
Chorus Director: Mr. Adam J. Hightower-Moreno
Concertmistress: Aimee Petersen, violin (until end of 2021); Bonnie Diggs, violin (since 2022)

Houston Masterworks Chorus: Beethoven: Saturday, October 16, 2021 (canceled)
Hauntcert 2021: Saturday, October 30, 2021
Deck the Halls 2021: Sunday, December 5, 2021
Musical Fates: Sunday, March 13, 2022
Beethoven 9: Sunday, May 1, 2022
Children's Concert: Doodles: Saturday, June 4, 2022
Freedom Rings 2022: Monday, July 4, 2022

Freedom Rings 2022

Monday, July 4, 2022
[7:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

Freedom Rings is an annual 4th of July (Independence Day) concert performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra. It was performed on July 4th at the Stafford Centre in the evening every year regardless of weekday. The Freedom Rings Concert is free for everyone, so people who are invited to this concert are welcome.

There was no intermission in this concert, because the City of Stafford does not want an intermission for the 4th of July Concert.

Children's Concert: Doodles

Saturday, June 4, 2022
[11:00 AM @ George Memorial Library]

Children's Concert is an annual concert performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra. It was taken place at George Memorial Library in the morning. The concert was free, so people who were invited to this concert are welcome.

The Children's Concert by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra was performed for the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic-related cancellations in 2020 and 2021.

There was no one-time intermission for this concert, because the Children's Concert was short that the orchestra performed up to one hour or less.

Beethoven 9

Sunday, May 1, 2022
[2:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

The May concert this season was titled "Beethoven 9". Only one piece was performed for this concert: a multi-movement symphony.

There was no one-time intermission for this concert due to performing only one piece with four movements straight; no intermission was held between the movements of the whole symphony.

Musical Fates

Sunday, March 13, 2022
[2:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

The spring concert this season was titled "Musical Fates".

A one-time intermission was held for this concert between the fourth and fifth pieces in concert order, both of those were concerto pieces with a large grand piano in front of the stage.

Concerto Winners

Deck the Halls 2021

Sunday, December 5, 2021
[2:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

The Deck the Halls concert is an annual Christmas and holiday concert performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra and Chorus at the Stafford Centre. In addition, there were two concerto winners performed for this concert, since the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra did not perform at least one concerto piece earlier in 2021 due to pandemic concerns in the Houston area.

First Deck the Halls concert taking place in person with invited guests since the COVID-19 pandemic that made the concert virtual last year.

A one-time intermission was held for this concert between the sixth and seventh pieces, both of them were concerto pieces with a large grand piano in front of the stage.

Concerto Winners

Hauntcert 2021

Saturday, October 30, 2021
[6:00 PM @ Pearland Town Center]

Mr. Bill Tackett, the assistant conductor of the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra, conducted all the pieces for this concert. This was the first concert performed for the 2021-2022 season, as the Houston Masterworks concert was canceled this season.

There was no one-time intermission for this concert, because the concert was so short that the assistant conductor Mr. Tackett wanted to run the concert up to one hour.

Houston Masterworks Chorus: Beethoven

Saturday, October 16, 2021 (canceled)

The collaboration between the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra and the Houston Masterworks Chorus for October 16 has been canceled, because HMC has decided to go to another direction with the concert on that day. This was a change of plan for HMC.

item.title: Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra: 2022–2023: Season 31
item.dc:creator: allenacnguyen
item.content:encoded:
These are the list of concerts performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra and Chorus for the 2022–2023 season, the 31st season. There were five concerts performed this season.

Music Director and Conductor: Dr. Dominique Royem, D.M.A.
Assistant Conductor: Mr. William "Bill" Tackett
Chorus Director: Mr. Ray Rhoads
Assistant Chorus Director: Mr. Steve Kalke
Concertmistress: Bonnie Diggs, violin

Death and Rebirth: Sunday, October 2, 2022
Hauntcert 2022: Saturday, October 29, 2022
Deck the Halls 2022: Sunday, December 4, 2022
Beethoven's Romantic Legacy: Sunday, June 4, 2023 (canceled)
Children's Concert: The Thrill of the Orchestra: Saturday, June 24, 2023
Freedom Rings 2023: Tuesday, July 4, 2023

Freedom Rings 2023

Tuesday, July 4, 2023
[7:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

Freedom Rings is an annual 4th of July (Independence Day) concert performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra. It was performed on July 4th at the Stafford Centre every year regardless of weekday. The Freedom Rings Concert is free for everyone, so people who are invited to this concert are welcome.

There was no intermission in this concert, because the City of Stafford does not want an intermission for the 4th of July Concert.

In addition, some pieces for this concert program were added from the previous two concerts.

Children's Concert: The Thrill of the Orchestra

Saturday, June 24, 2023
[11:00 AM @ George Memorial Library]

Children's Concert is an annual concert that is hosted and performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra. It was held at George Memorial Library. The concert is free for everyone, so people who are invited to this concert are welcome.

There was no intermission for this concert, because the Children's Concert was too short and the duration of the concert lasted one hour or less.

Mr. Ray Rhoads, the Chorus Director of the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra and Chorus, narrated this concert.

Beethoven's Romantic Legacy

Sunday, June 4, 2023 (canceled)

This concert was about how composers after Ludwig van Beethoven reacted to his being as a powerful, important composer. There were no pieces composed by Beethoven himself for this concert.

This concert was meant to replace the canceled Worhol concert in March this season due to unforeseen circumstances with the Worhol band.

This concert was originally scheduled to be on Sunday, March 12, 2023, at the Stafford Centre at 2:00 PM. However, due to extremely low ticket sales, this concert was postponed to May 14, 2023 (Mother's Day) as decided by the board. This date move led to the opera concert being moved to March of next season. March 12, 2023 was a bad concert to date due to the start of spring break. Then, the board pushed the concert date again to May 21, 2023, with a venue set at B.F. Terry High School, as the organization was trepidatious about performing the concert on Mother's Day. The concert date was then, pushed again to May 28, 2023, due to B.F. Terry High School forgot to register for the graduation ceremony on May 21. Again, it was pushed to Sunday, June 4, 2023, that May 28 was the Sunday before Memorial Day, which could lead to another fiasco in performing on Memorial Day weekend if the building were to be closed on that weekend. June 4 was the last date change for this concert, and the venue was yet to be determined with venue availability of B.F. Terry High School being uncertain on this day.

Without a certain venue (other than Stafford Centre and B.F. Terry High School) to be determined soon enough on June 4, 2023, this concert has been canceled. The board of the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra gave up the search for a different venue after a long discussion and a series of concert date changes. The reason behind this concert cancellation is because the organization was too close to the concert date to sell tickets effectively. The music director and the board did not act swiftly enough during the month of May 2023 to find an available venue for this concert to still happen. The attempt to find an available venue for this concert after the concert date change was a failure to this organization this season.

In addition, a one-time intermission would have been held for this concert between pieces.

Concerto Winners

Some of these pieces of this canceled concert were made up in later concerts:

  • Berlioz's Hungarian March and Liszt's Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2 were both made up and performed for the Freedom Rings (4th of July) concert this season.
  • The Brahms' Tragic Overture was made up and performed in the March concert of next season (actually held on February 18, 2024). That concert was titled An Afternoon of Romance, which happened as a second romantic concert after the canceled Beethoven's Romantic Legacy concert.
  • The concerto winners of 2023 have been moved to the Deck the Halls concert of next season. The only concerto piece made up this year was the third movement of Mendelssohn's Piano Concerto No. 1, performed by 2023 HMTA Concerto Winner Shangen Zou of the Junior Division. It was the only concerto piece performed this year. The other two concerto pieces that have yet to be performed were the first movement of Brahms' Piano Concerto No. 1 and all four movements of Liszt's Piano Concerto No. 1.

Deck the Halls 2022

Sunday, December 4, 2022
[2:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

The Deck the Halls concert is an annual Christmas and holiday concert performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra and Chorus at the Stafford Centre. There were no concerto pieces performed for this concert since they don't have any concerto winners to play for the remainder of the year 2022.

A one-time intermission was held at this concert between the sixth and seventh pieces in order.

Hauntcert 2022

Saturday, October 29, 2022
[6:00 PM @ Pearland Town Center]

This concert was performed in one hour. There was no intermission for this concert, because the concert was too short and the duration of the concert lasted for up to one hour.

This concert was free to attend because it was taken place outdoors, so people who are invited are welcome.

Death and Rebirth

Sunday, October 2, 2022
[2:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

This concert was originally scheduled in March but moved to October in place of the Worhol concert. There were no concerto pieces performed for this concert.

A one-time intermission was held for this concert between the fourth and fifth pieces in concert order. Shostakovich's Symphony No. 5 was the only piece performed for the second half of this concert.

These are the list of concerts performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra and Chorus for the 2023–2024 season, the 32nd season.

Music Director and Conductor: Dr. Dominique Royem, D.M.A.

An Afternoon of Romance: Sunday, February 18, 2024

Travel Postcards: Pictures at an Exhibition: Saturday, May 11, 2024
Freedom Rings 2024: Thursday, July 4, 2024

Freedom Rings 2024

Thursday, July 4, 2024
[7:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

Freedom Rings is an annual 4th of July (Independence Day) concert performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra. It was performed on July 4th at the Stafford Centre in the evening every year regardless of weekday. The Freedom Rings Concert is free for everyone, so people who are invited to this concert are welcome.

There was no intermission for this concert, because the City of Stafford does not want an intermission for the 4th of July Concert.

Pieces cut from program

Travel Postcards: Pictures at an Exhibition

Saturday, May 11, 2024
[7:30 PM @ Clements High School]

The May concert this season was titled "Travel Postcards: Pictures at an Exhibition."

There was a one-time intermission for this concert between the third and fourth pieces in order.

UPDATE 3/15/2024: The program for the May concert this season has been changed, because the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra for "An Evening at the Opera" concert was priced out of Houston Christian University's Dunham Theatre due to some sort of high rates that it is too expensive to afford.

UPDATE 3/24/2024: The venue has been booked for this concert. It was held at Clements High School in Fort Bend ISD in the auditorium.

Children's Concert: Behold the Umbrellaphant!

Saturday, March 23, 2024
[10:30 AM @ George Memorial Library]

Children’s Concert is an annual concert that is hosted and performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra. It will be held at George Memorial Library annually in either March or June. The Children's Concert this season will be in March. The concert is free for everyone, so people who are invited to this concert are welcome. Since this concert will be held in the morning, George Memorial Library will be open at 10:00 AM with the doors open.

There will be no intermission for this concert, because Children's Concert is too short and the duration of the concert will be one hour or less.

The narrators will be Mr. Tackett for Behold the Bold Umbrellaphant and Dr. Royem for The Itsy Bitsy Spider and His Great Singalong Adventure since Mr. Rhoads will not be available to narrate for this concert.

An Afternoon of Romance

Sunday, February 18, 2024
[2:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

This concert was also known as "The Romantics". This concert was fulfilled from the cancelled "Beethoven's Romantic Legacy" concert in June last year with the Brahms' Tragic Overture added to the program.

The exceptions from the cancelled concert last year were Schubert's Unfinished Symphony and Schumann's Manfred Overture, which there was not enough room to play both of these pieces for this season nor for this concert. Both of these pieces could be made up next season if the Music Director of the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra agree.

There was a one-time intermission for this concert between the third and fourth pieces in order.

The elevator in front of the stage in the auditorium of Stafford Centre was broken at the time this concert was held, which is why the floor section in front of the stage was missing.

Concerto Winners

Deck the Halls 2023

Sunday, December 3, 2023
[2:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

The Deck the Halls concert is an annual Christmas and holiday concert performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra and Chorus at the Stafford Centre. In addition, there was only one concerto winner performed for this concert, since the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra did not perform at least one concerto piece earlier in 2023.

A one-time intermission was held at this concert between the eighth and ninth pieces in concert order, right after the concerto with a large grand piano in front of the stage and before getting on to Christmas pieces in the second half of the concert.

Concerto Winners

Concerto Winners not in program

Hauntcert 2023

Saturday, October 28, 2023
[5:00 PM @ Pearland Town Center]

Hauntcert is an annual concert performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra, and it took place at Pearland Town Center in late afternoon hours or by evening. This concert was free to attend because it was taken place outdoors, so people who were invited are welcome.

This concert was performed in one hour. There was no intermission for this concert, because the concert was too short.

The guest conductors for this concert were Stephen Crawford and David Flores, since Dr. Dominique Royem and Mr. Bill Tackett both had weddings during the weekend of this concert.

Conductor: Stephen Crawford, Freelance Conductor
Assistant Conductor: David Flores, Principal Trombone

Straight from the Soundtrack: Westerns

Sunday, October 8, 2023
[2:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

The fall concert this season was titled "Straight from the Soundtrack: Westerns". It covers pieces that was heard from some Westerns films.

There was a one-time intermission during the concert between the ninth and tenth pieces in concert order.

item.title: Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra: 2024–2025: Season 33
item.dc:creator: allenacnguyen
item.content:encoded:
These are the list of concerts that will be performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra and Chorus for the 2024–2025 season, the 33rd season.

Music Director and Conductor: Dr. Dominique Royem, D.M.A.
Assistant Conductor: Mr. William “Bill” Tackett
Chorus Director: Mr. Ray Rhoads
Assistant Chorus Director: Mr. Steve Kalke
Concertmistress: Bonnie Diggs, violin

—

Also, this was the last season for William "Bill" Tackett to serve as an assistant conductor for the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra before becoming a music director with another symphony orchestra somewhere in Houston.

An Afternoon at the Opera: Sunday, October 20, 2024
Hauntcert 2024: Saturday, October 26, 2024
Deck the Halls 2024: Sunday, December 8, 2024
Sugar Land Mayor's Concert: Date Changed
WFBSO: Sounds of the 60's: Sunday, March 9, 2025
Children's Concert: Orchestra Games: Saturday, April 12, 2025
I Dream a World: Chorus Orchestra Concert: Saturday, May 17, 2025
Freedom Rings 2025: Friday, July 4, 2025

Freedom Rings 2025

Friday, July 4, 2025
[7:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

Freedom Rings is an annual 4th of July (Independence Day) concert performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra. It was performed on July 4th at the Stafford Centre every year regardless of weekday. The Freedom Rings Concert is free for everyone, so people who are invited to this concert are welcome.

Like the previous 4th of July concerts with the FBSOC, there was no intermission for this concert, because the City of Stafford does not want an intermission for the 4th of July Concert.

—

I Dream a World: Chorus Orchestra Concert

Saturday, May 17, 2025
[7:00 PM @ First United Methodist Church Missouri City]

The title for the May concert this season is I Dream a World: Chorus Orchestra Concert. Originally, the concert title was Songs of Hope and Peace.

The choir, the Fort Bend Symphony Chorus, will sing for this concert. This is a chorus concert.

No concerto winners performed for the May concert this season.

There was a one-time intermission held for this concert. The intermission was held right after the sixth piece that marked the end of the first half of the concert.

—

Children's Concert: Orchestra Games

Saturday, April 12, 2025
[10:30 AM @ George Memorial Library]

Children’s Concert is an annual concert that is hosted and performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra. It is held at George Memorial Library annually; either in late March, early April, or June, depending on George Memorial Library to give the music director Dr. Royem the date of availability. The concert is free for everyone, so people who are invited to this concert are welcome. Since this concert was held on Saturday morning, George Memorial Library was open at 10:00 AM with the library doors open.

The title for the Children's Concert this season is Orchestra Games.

There was no intermission for this concert, because the Children's Concert is too short and the duration of the concert will be up to one hour or less.

—

WFBSO: Sounds of the 60's

Sunday, March 9, 2025
[2:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

The title for the March concert this season will be WFBSO: Sounds of the 60's. The Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra has another installment of their radio show, WFBSO. This concert took place at the Stafford Centre.

For this concert based on the radio program, there was a DJ (disc jockey) to play with the orchestra. The DJ was Mr. Rhoads, the Chorus Director of the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra Chorus. There will also be a pianist playing the electric keyboard with different instrumentation in some of the pieces for this concert.

Additionally, there was a concerto winner to perform for this concert. One from Marielle Ogletree Young Artists concerto competition of 2025.

There was a one-time intermission held for this concert. The intermission was held right after the concerto piece that marked the end of the first half of the concert.

—

Concerto Winners

Sugar Land Mayor's Concert

Date Changed
[Time TBA @ Smart Financial Center]

The Sugar Land Mayor's Concert has changed, per the music director of the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra. The Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra was slated to perform for this special mayor's concert on Tuesday, March 4, 2025 at the Smart Financial Center, but the date has changed. So, they are focusing with the music on the Sounds of the 60's concert instead.

Deck the Halls 2024

Sunday, December 8, 2024
[2:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

The Deck the Halls concert is an annual Christmas and holiday concert performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra and Chorus at the Stafford Centre. It was held on the first Sunday in December in the afternoon as usual. In addition, there was at least one concerto winner to play for this Deck the Halls concert.

The special occasion about this concert was that the chorus from three different middle choirs sung some Christmas pieces for this concert.

A one-time intermission was held at this concert between pieces, right after the concerto piece to end the first half of the concert.

—

Concerto Winners

Hauntcert 2024

Saturday, October 26, 2024
[5:00 PM @ Pearland Town Center]

Hauntcert is an annual Halloween concert performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra, and it will take place at Pearland Town Center in late afternoon hours or by evening. This concert will be free to attend because it will be taken place outdoors, so people who are invited are welcome.

Additionally, some members of the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra were dressed up in costumes for this concert.

This concert was performed up to one hour. There was no intermission for this concert, because the concert program was short up to an hour as expected.

—

An Afternoon at the Opera

Sunday, October 20, 2024
[2:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

The fall concert this season was the opera concert titled An Afternoon at the Opera, and it took place at the Stafford Centre. The chorus also sang for this concert, plus the two invited opera singers. Additionally, this concert had two concerto winners, both from HMTA this year.

There was a guest conductor for this concert named Dr. Julie Sorensen, who conducted some pieces in place of the current assistant conductor.

When it comes to an opera concert, the orchestra was set up on the stage in the auditorium of Stafford Centre. The opera singers to sing for this opera concert stood in front of the orchestra and on the raised platform of the elevator pit, per the music director. The names of opera singers for this concert are:

  • René Vazquez, tenor (N/A)
  • Dominique McCormick, soprano

This concert has been pushed to a later date several times due to the circumstances of previous concert changes from last year and this year:

  • The moving of Beethoven's Romantic Legacy concert last year from March to May, which was the reason why the opera concert was moved to March earlier this year.
  • The March concert earlier this year was replaced by An Afternoon of Romance (actually held on February 18) due to the cancellation of Beethoven's Romantic Legacy concert that was supposed to happen on June 4 last year, but no certain venue to be found. Being too close to the concert date without a certain venue led to the particular concert being canceled. This was the reason why the opera concert was pushed to May earlier this year.
  • The May concert earlier this year was replaced by Travel Postcards: Pictures at an Exhibition, due to the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra and Chorus being priced out of Dunham Theater at Houston Christian University for the organization to afford. This is the reason why the opera concert has been pushed to October this year, and the venue for this concert will now be at Stafford Centre that took place in the afternoon.

A one-time intermission was held for this concert between the two concerto pieces, marking the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half of the concert, respectively.

—

Concerto Winners

Pieces cut from program

item.title: Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra: 2025–2026: Season 34
item.dc:creator: allenacnguyen
item.content:encoded:
Page updated as of June 30, 2026.

Update reason: Complete 4th of July program information.

These are the list of concerts that will be performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra and Chorus for the 2025–2026 season, the 34th season.

Music Director and Conductor: Dr. Dominique Royem, D.M.A.
Principal Conductor: Dr. Julie Sorensen, Ph.D.
Chorus Director: Mr. Ray Rhoads
Assistant Chorus Director: Mr. Steve Kalke
Interim Chorus Director 2026: Dr. Demetrius Robinson, Ph.D.
Guest Choir Director: Dr. Ashton D. Jones, D.M.A.
Concertmistress: Bonnie Diggs, violin

This is the first season where Dr. Julie Sorensen will serve as the Principal Conductor of the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra and Chorus, the first in organization's history, replacing Mr. William "Bill" Tackett as the assistant conductor. Dr. Sorensen served as the Guest Conductor of this organization conducting only for "An Afternoon of the Opera" concert in the previous season.

Road Trip Across America: Sunday, October 19, 2025
Hauntcert 2025: Saturday, October 25, 2025 (canceled)
Deck the Halls 2025: Sunday, December 7, 2025
Tango!: Sunday, March 15, 2026
A Joyful Chorus: Saturday, April 18, 2026
Children's Concert: The Magic of Music: Saturday, May 23, 2026
Freedom Rings 2026: Saturday, July 4, 2026

Freedom Rings 2026

Saturday, July 4, 2026
[7:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

Freedom Rings is an annual 4th of July (Independence Day) concert performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra. It was performed on July 4th at the Stafford Centre every year regardless of weekday. The Freedom Rings Concert is free for everyone, so people who are invited to this concert are welcome.

2026 will mark the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence of the United States of America. This is also known as the United States Semiquincentennial. The chorus will also sing for the 250th anniversary performance along with the orchestra.

Like the previous 4th of July concerts with the FBSOC, there will be no intermission for this concert, because the City of Stafford does not want an intermission for the 4th of July Concert.

The list of pieces for this concert is not yet confirmed. It will be under proposal once the music director is ready to list which pieces will be performed for this concert after the May concert or the Children's concert.

Children's Concert: The Magic of Music

Saturday, May 23, 2026
[10:30 AM @ George Memorial Library]

Children’s Concert is an annual concert that is hosted and performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra. It will be held at George Memorial Library annually. The concert is free for everyone, so people who are invited to this concert are welcome. Since this concert will be held in the morning, George Memorial Library will be open at 10:00 AM with the doors open. The concert will begin at 10:30 AM.

The title for the Children's Concert in 2026 is The Magic of Music.

Dr. Sorensen will be leading the Children's Concert for this season. Dr. Royem will be the cellist for this concert.

There was no intermission for this concert, because the Children's Concert was too short and the duration of the concert was up to one hour or less.

A Joyful Chorus

Saturday, April 18, 2026
[7:30 PM @ First United Methodist Church Missouri City]

The title for the chorus orchestra concert this season was "A Joyful Chorus." Dr. Robinson, the interim chorus director for the Fort Bend Symphony Chorus, led and programmed this concert.

  • Dr. Dominique Royem, D.M.A.; Music Director/Conductor
  • Dr. Julie Sorensen, Ph.D.; Principal Conductor
  • Dr. Demetrius Robinson, Ph.D.; Interim Chorus Director
  • Dr. Ashton D. Jones, D.M.A.; Guest Choir Director

The choir, the Fort Bend Symphony Chorus, sang for most of this concert. This chorus concert was accompanied by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra. Dr. Royem was a cellist for this concert, as she conducted just the Borodin Symphony.

There was no intermission for this concert, because the FBSO director Dr. Royem said the orchestra and chorus were playing straight through in a single concert session.

^ Orchestra only
† Chorus only

Tango!

Sunday, March 15, 2026
[2:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

The title for the Spring 2026 concert this season was titled "Tango!".

This concert featured an Argentinian guest conductor Martín García León.

One concerto winner played for this concert.

A one-time intermission for this concert was held between Ginastera's suite and Prokofiev's concerto.

Concerto Winners

Deck the Halls 2025

Sunday, December 7, 2025
[2:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

The Deck the Halls concert is an annual Christmas and holiday concert that is performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra and Chorus at the Stafford Centre. It was held on the first Sunday in December in the afternoon as usual.

The Fort Bend Symphony Chorus sang for this concert like the past Deck the Halls concerts.

A one-time intermission was held at this concert between 8th and 9th pieces in concert order.

Concerto Winners (NOT PLAYED)

Hauntcert 2025

Saturday, October 25, 2025 (canceled)
[Time N/A @ (no venue determined)]

Hauntcert is an annual Halloween concert performed by the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra, and it usually take place on the last Saturday in October.

NOTE: The Hauntcert for this season has been canceled due to Pearland Town Center canceling the Halloween event in 2025. There was no sponsor for the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra to find a venue soon enough for the Hauntcert to happen.

Additionally, some members of the Fort Bend Symphony Orchestra would have dressed up in costumes for this concert.

This concert would have performed up to one hour. It was likely that there will not be an intermission for this concert, because the concert would have been short up to an hour as expected.

Road Trip Across America

Sunday, October 19, 2025
[2:00 PM @ Stafford Centre]

The title of the fall concert this season, usually in October, was Road Trip Across America. This concert took place at the Stafford Centre as the first concert of the season.

Additionally, this concert had two concerto winners, both from the HMTA in 2025.

The vocal soloist for this concert was Dominique McCormick, a soprano who performed in "An Afternoon at the Opera" concert last season.

A one-time intermission was held for this concert between the concerto pieces.

Concerto Winners

item.title: Constituent Proposal: Articles of Impeachment against President Trump
item.dc:creator: allenacnguyen
item.content:encoded:
I, Allen-Tri Hai Nguyen, an independent citizen and politics enthusiast from Houston, TX, propose articles of impeachment to impeach the President of the United States, Donald John Trump, for high crimes and misdemeanors when Democrats take majority of the House of Representatives and the Senate after 2026 midterm elections.

Potential Articles of Impeachment that President Trump would be accused of during his second administration (2025–present as the 47th U.S. President):

  • Article I: Abuse of Power
  • Article II: Deprivation of Civil Rights
  • Article III: Deprivation of Due Process
  • Article IV: Dereliction of Duty
  • Article V: Obstruction of Political Officials
  • Article VI: Obstruction of Congress
  • Article VII: Obstruction of Justice
  • Article VIII: Incitement and Threats against Political Opposition
  • Article IX: Reckless Endangerment of Public Safety
  • Article X: Usurpation of War Powers
  • Article XI: Reckless Endangerment of Economic Fallout
  • Article XII: Incitement to Sovereign Genocide
  • Article XIII: Misuse of Public Funds
  • Article XIV: Flouting the Leahy Law

President Donald Trump was already impeached twice during his first presidency (2017-2021 as the 45th U.S. President).

  • 1st Impeachment (2019): Call with Ukrainian President Zelensky to investigate Joe Biden
    • Article I: Abuse of Power
      • House Vote: 230—197
      • Senate Vote: 48—52
    • Article II: Obstruction of Congress
      • House Vote: 229—198
      • Senate Vote: 47—53
    • Result: Acquitted. President remains in office.
      —
  • 2nd Impeachment (2021): January 6, 2021 Capitol riot
    • Article I: Incitement of Insurrection
      • House Vote: 232—197
      • Senate Vote: 57—43
    • Result: Acquitted

The potential third impeachment of President Trump would be a compendium of broader issues during his second administration.

Summary of the Articles of Impeachment for the potential third impeachment of President Trump

Evidentiary Breakdown

The Operational Nexus: Linking Noem to Trump [Articles I & VI]

The Operation Midway Blitz & Operation Metro Surge Execution

  • As DHS Secretary, Noem held direct operational command over ICE and CBP. Under her leadership, these agencies shifted from traditional administrative enforcement into high-intensity, military-style urban occupations. The execution of warrantless residential raids, the implementation of "collateral arrests," and the aggressive tactics used during Operation Midway Blitz in Chicago were direct results of operational directives flowing from Noem’s desk—authorized by the White House.

The Shield of the Americas Appointment (The Conspiracy Loop)

  • The definitive proof of a coordinated executive conspiracy culminates on March 24, 2026. Facing intense scrutiny, congressional hearings, and looming impeachment pressure from Democratic lawmakers for her heavy-handed tactics and the tragic deaths of U.S. citizens (Silverio Villegas González, Renée Good, and Alex Pretti), Trump fired her as DHS Secretary.
    —
  • However, instead of distancing the administration from her malpractices, Trump immediately established a new, unvetted position and appointed her as the United States Special Envoy for the Shield of the Americas in the Western Hemisphere. A Democratic House majority would frame this rapid reappointment as a calculated move to shield Noem from immediate congressional accountability, reward her for executing the administration's aggressive domestic agenda, and keep her within the executive orbit out of reach of legislative oversight.

Noem's Malpractice Time Block

  • January 25, 2025: Appointed as DHS Secretary; begins immediate restructuring of ICE/CBP operational mandates.
  • Winter 2025–2026: Authorizes Operation Midway Blitz and Operation Metro Surge, bypassing traditional Article III judicial warrants and initiating widespread domestic collateral arrests.
  • March 2026: Actively obstructs congressional oversight by refusing to supply internal DHS operational memos or answer for the 40+ custody deaths during recent House committee hearings.
  • March 24, 2026: Terminated by President Trump under intense public and legislative impeachment pressure.
  • Spring 2026: Immediately installed by executive decree as Special Envoy for the Shield of the Americas, maintaining executive privilege protection and avoiding standard legislative vetting.

The “Chain of Command” Callout Block

"The immediate creation of an unvetted Envoy position to harbor a terminated, highly controversial Cabinet Secretary provides clear, documented evidence of an intentional executive effort to evade the oversight mechanisms of the United States Congress."

Master Specifications [Articles II & III]

SPECIFICATION I (Operation Midway Blitz): In executing a multi-agency sweep codenamed "Operation Midway Blitz" in Chicago, Illinois, the administration did authorize federal agents to bypass Article III judicial warrants, conduct mass warrantless raids on domestic households, and engage in the unlawful, suspicionless "collateral arrest" of residents, directly resulting in the unconstitutional detention of United States citizens and culminating in the tragic, extrajudicial death of Silverio Villegas González.

SPECIFICATION II (Operation Metro Surge): In executing a paramilitary municipal occupation codenamed "Operation Metro Surge" in Minneapolis, Minnesota, the administration did deliberately suspend standard constitutional due process, leading to the unlawful, race-based profiling and detention of documented individuals, and the reckless deployment of lethal force by federal agents on domestic soil that resulted in the fatal shootings of Renée Good on January 7, 2026, and Alex Pretti on January 24, 2026.

Master Specification: Weaponization and Shielding of DHS Leadership |
SPECIFICATION III (DHS Paramilitary Command and Oversight Obstruction):
In violation of his constitutional oath, the President did appoint and maintain Kristi Noem (R-SD) as Secretary of Homeland Security, actively directing and permitting her to convert the Department of Homeland Security, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) into a de facto paramilitary force tasked with violating the civil liberties of individuals on American soil; and did further obstruct the Legislative Branch by abruptly terminating said Secretary amid intense congressional scrutiny on March 24, 2026, only to immediately bypass standard Senate confirmation channels by appointing her as Special Envoy for the Shield of the Americas, thereby intentionally insulating her from legislative oversight, suppressing vital operational evidence, and perpetuating an executive conspiracy to abuse federal power.

Injected Incident Factual Specifications [Articles IV, V, & VI]

Factual Specification A (Article IV: Dereliction of Duty):
The administration permitted a culture of gross medical neglect and hazardous containment across federal facilities, leading to the December 2025 custody death of 41-year-old Jean Wilson Brutus at Delaney Hall within 24 hours of his arrival, and directly prompting the May 2026 coordinated hunger and labor strike of over 300 detainees protesting worm-infested food, lack of potable water, and untreated tuberculosis outbreaks. By ignoring documented systemic patterns of fatalities and retaliating against striking detainees with solitary confinement, the Executive willfully inflicted cruel and unusual punishment under color of law.

Factual Specification B (Article V: Obstruction of Political Officials):
The administration repeatedly weaponized the Department of Homeland Security to assault the sovereignty of state and local leaders. This pattern is demonstrated by the May 9, 2025, physical arrest and trespassing charges brought against Newark Mayor Ras Baraka (D) outside Delaney Hall after the city filed a lawsuit challenging the facility's local safety codes, and the May 2026 physical blocking of New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill (D-NJ), who was denied access to inspect the state's public health conditions inside the facility, forcing her to deploy state police to establish a protected zone against federal agents.

Factual Specification C [Articles V (Obstruction of Political Officials) & VI (Obstruction of Congress)]:
The Executive Branch deliberately used physical violence and criminal intimidation to paralyze congressional oversight. During the May 2026 civil unrest at Delaney Hall, federal agents in tactical gear deployed chemical weapons, directly pepper-spraying United States Senator Andy Kim (D-NJ) as he attempted to observe a public demonstration and inspect the facility. This acts in tandem with the administration's retaliatory, weaponized federal grand jury indictment of United States Representative LaMonica McIver (D-NJ), who faces a 17-year sentence on trumped-up charges of "interfering with federal officers" simply for attempting to conduct a legal congressional oversight inspection of the facility.
—

The Assault on Federalism & Municipal Sovereignty [Article V]

  • Mayor Ras Baraka (D-Newark, NJ): Arrested by federal agents outside an ICE detention facility in his own city. This represents a direct assault on local municipal sovereignty, using federal force to strip a local chief executive of his freedom for challenging federal actions on his own soil.
    —
  • Comptroller Brad Lander (D-NYC, NY): Arrested at an ICE detention facility in the NY/NJ region while carrying out his public duties as a fiscal watchdog and elected official. This demonstrates an intentional pattern of detaining fiscal and administrative oversight officials to deter public scrutiny of federal facilities.
    —
  • Governor Mikie Sherrill (D-NJ): Physically blocked by federal agents from accessing the Delaney Hall facility during a unfolding public health and civil rights crisis. This constitutes a direct violation of the Tenth Amendment, using federal paramilitary forces to unlawfully override a state governor’s public health police power and jurisdiction.

The Violent Disruption of Co-Equal Legislative Power [Articles V & VI]

  • Senator Alex Padilla (D-CA): Forcibly removed and handcuffed by federal agents during a public press conference held by DHS Secretary Kristi Noem in Los Angeles. This acts as a highly visible, public humiliation of a sitting United States Senator, designed to signal to the nation that the administration would not tolerate legislative presence or dissent within executive spaces.
    —
  • Senator Andy Kim (D-NJ): Directly pepper-sprayed in the face by federal tactical agents outside Delaney Hall while attempting to observe a civil demonstration and conduct an emergent oversight check. This is an unprecedented act of physical violence committed by executive agents against a sitting member of the United States Senate, crossing a critical constitutional red line.
    —
  • Representative LaMonica McIver (D-NJ): Indicted by a weaponized federal grand jury on charges of "forcibly impeding and interfering with federal officers," facing a retaliatory 17-year prison sentence simply for executing a legal congressional oversight visit at Delaney Hall. This represents the ultimate weaponization of the federal criminal justice system, attempting to use the threat of long-term imprisonment to permanently freeze the House’s constitutional oversight capabilities.

The Epstein Nexus: The Invisible Track of Article VI (Obstruction of Congress)

While the physical intimidation of lawmakers took place on the steps of detention centers, the concealment of the Epstein files represents an identical effort to paralyze the co-equal branch of government through administrative obstruction.

  • The Intent to Obstruct: The House Judiciary Committee would argue that the mass redactions executed under former Attorney General Pam Bondi were not standard privacy protections, but a coordinated executive operation to sanitize the Epstein Files Transparency Act (EFTA) documents before they reached Congress.
    —
  • The High Crime: By systematically expunging the names of high-profile political individuals, cabinet members, and President Trump himself, the Executive Branch actively blinded the House Oversight Committee. Defying the subsequent April 14, 2026, subpoena was the final act of this strategy, ensuring that the true nature of the administration's links to international sex trafficking remained shielded from legislative investigation.

Cover Block

ADMINISTRATIVE OVERRIDE: Tracking the Subversion of the Epstein Files Transparency Act.

The Legal Anatomy of the Epstein Cover-Up [Article VII]:

  • The Catalyst (The EFTA Subversion): On November 19, 2025, President Trump signed the Epstein Files Transparency Act (EFTA), a piece of legislation near-unanimously demanded by Congress and the public. However, instead of executing the law faithfully, the administration allegedly treated it as an intelligence screening tool to identify and neutralize legal vulnerabilities.
    —
  • The Weaponization of the DOJ: Under the direction of Attorney General Pam Bondi, the DOJ was systematically weaponized to manage the document release. Rather than providing transparency, Bondi oversaw a massive redaction campaign. The House oversight committee would allege that these redactions were specifically designed to expunge the names of high-profile co-conspirators, cabinet members, and President Trump himself, protecting the administration from exposure regarding past ties to Epstein’s network.
    —
  • The Cover-Up Collapses: The crisis escalated to an impeachment tier when survivors and victims of Epstein’s abuse testified in public congressional hearings, directly contradicting the DOJ's redacted narratives. As the political heat intensified, President Trump abruptly fired Pam Bondi on April 2, 2026—an action the House would frame as an attempt to distance the White House from the cover-up and silence Bondi before she could be fully cross-examined.

The Direct Track to Impeachment: Subpoena Defiance

The tipping point that transforms this scandal into an explicit Article of Impeachment is Bondi's direct defiance of the Legislative Branch after her firing, acting as a proxy to protect the President.

  • The April 14, 2026 No-Show: Following her termination, the House Judiciary Committee issued a deposition subpoena to Bondi to uncover who ordered the redactions. Bondi executed a total "no-show," refusing to appear or hand over unredacted DOJ communications.
    —
  • The Contempt Filings: On April 29, 2026, Representative Robert Garcia (D-CA) filed formal contempt of Congress charges against Bondi. Even though she eventually submitted to a closed-door hearing on May 29, 2026, under the weight of those criminal charges, the House would use discovered evidence and her initial obstruction to prove a coordinated executive conspiracy to impede a federal investigation.

Evidentiary Timeline Block

  • November 19, 2025: EFTA signed into law under immense public pressure.
  • Winter 2025–2026: DOJ/Bondi systematically redact key administration and cabinet identifiers.
  • Spring 2026: Public testimony from Epstein survivors exposes inconsistencies in redacted files.
  • April 2, 2026: Trump fires Bondi to disrupt the chain of accountability.
  • April 14, 2026: Bondi defies a congressional subpoena, prompting Rep. Garcia's April 29 contempt filing.
  • May 29, 2026: Closed-door testimony reveals internal White House pressure directives.

The “Smoking Gun” Text Callout

“The primary beneficiary of the Department of Justice's (DOJ) redactions and Bondi's subsequent subpoena defiance was the President of the United States.”

Article IX (Reckless Endangerment of Public Safety) Supporting Case

Primary Exhibit: Internal DHS Directives and Airport Security Logs detailing operational chaos and passenger tracking data during the TSA/ICE checkpoint transition.

  • ⚠️ Aviation Vulnerability: Total degradation of standard TSA baggage and passenger screening matrices due to zero certified training among substitute ICE personnel.
    —
  • 🛑 Civil Liberty Hazards: Multiple recorded incidents of ICE agents attempting to conduct arbitrary identity checks, immigration status verification, and warrantless secondary searches on domestic travelers inside standard domestic terminals.
    —
  • 📉 Economic/Structural Paralysis: Massive operational delays, missed flights, and terminal closures that compounded the domestic economic strain alongside the ongoing shutdown.

Legal Analysis of the War Powers Breach [Article X]

  • The Constitutional Core: Under Article I, Section 8, Clause 11 (The War Powers Clause), the Framers explicitly granted the exclusive authority to initiate offensive military conflict to the Legislative Branch, not the Executive. The President’s role as Commander-in-Chief under Article II is strictly defensive—meant to repel sudden attacks against the United States, not to unilaterally initiate offensive wars or assassinate foreign heads of state.
    —
  • The Statutory Violation: Both operations represent a textbook violation of the War Powers Resolution of 1973 (50 U.S.C. §§ 1541–1548). The law strictly dictates that the President can only introduce U.S. Armed Forces into hostilities under three specific conditions: (1) a formal declaration of war, (2) specific statutory authorization (an AUMF), or (3) a national emergency created by an attack upon the United States. Neither the regime in Venezuela nor the leadership in Iran had launched an attack on U.S. soil, meaning the President acted completely outside the law.

Legal Anatomy of the Tariff Slush Fund [Article XIII]

The Revenue Seizure (The Breach of the Taxing Clause)

  • Under Article I, Section 8, Clause 1, Congress holds the exclusive power to lay and collect taxes, duties, and imposts. While statutes like Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act allow the President to levy tariffs for genuine national security emergencies, using them to deliberately engineer domestic revenue outside the budget process is an unconstitutional usurpation of legislative authority.

The Spend Mechanism (The Slush Fund creation)

  • When billions of dollars in unilateral tariff penalties are collected from international trade routes, the administration does not route them through standard congressional appropriations. Instead, the Executive Branch funnels these billions into specialized, off-budget accounts (such as the Commodity Credit Corporation or newly engineered DHS operational accounts). Because the Executive completely controls the distribution of these accounts, they become a multi-billion-dollar presidential slush fund.

Three-Column Comparison
The Transnational Slush Fund Engine (Article XIII Evidence)

Bold Monetary Callouts

  • Off-Budget Slush Funds
  • Reprogrammed Capital
  • Unlawful Revenue Generation

Legal Mechanics of the Leahy Law [Article XIV]

  • The Statutory Command: Named after Senator Patrick Leahy, the Leahy Law (Section 620M of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 and parallel Department of Defense statutes) places a strict, non-negotiable prohibition on the U.S. government. It dictates that no federal funds or security assistance may be provided to any unit of the security forces of a foreign country if the Secretary of State or Secretary of Defense has credible information that such unit has committed a Gross Violation of Human Rights (GVHR).
    —
  • The Standard of GVHR: Under federal and international definitions, GVHR explicitly includes acts of extrajudicial killing, torture, forced disappearance, or the deliberate engineering of mass civilian displacement and starvation.
    —
  • The Violation: The legal breach occurs because the Leahy Law does not grant the President "executive waiver" authority based on geopolitical convenience. Once credible evidence of GVHR exists — such as the staggering civilian casualty numbers and mass displacements documented by international oversight bodies in Gaza and Lebanon during the second Trump administration—the delivery of arms, logistics, and intelligence to those specific operational units becomes an explicit federal crime.

Incident Specifications

SPECIFICATION I (Systemic Vetting Failures): The administration did actively order the Department of State and the Department of Defense to alter, suspend, or bypass standard statutory "Leahy vetting" protocols to ensure that high-yield munitions, intelligence-sharing networks, and defensive systems were transferred to foreign units heavily implicated in the destruction of civilian infrastructure, medical facilities, and designated safe zones in Gaza and Lebanon.

SPECIFICATION II (Defiance of Oversight Evidence): The President did willfully ignore multiple formal "Leahy Law alerts" and classified human rights assessments generated by the State Department’s Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor (DRL), choosing instead to maintain direct, unvetted assistance to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s offensive, thereby transforming a mandatory statutory restriction into a discarded executive option.

Two-Column Block
Statutory Breach Archive: The Leahy Law Firewall (Article XIV)

Statutory Notice

“Political alignment with a foreign head of state does not grant the Executive Branch a license to violate domestic statutory laws passed by the United States Congress.”

Enforcement and Executive Summary

“Upon the convening of the 120th Congress in January 2027, the structural execution of these fourteen Articles of Impeachment shall be directed by Speaker Hakeem Jeffries, utilizing the full legislative and appropriations authority of the House rostrum to halt ongoing executive overreach. The evidentiary compilation and constitutional litigation of these charges shall be spearheaded by Representative Jamie Raskin via the House Committee on Oversight and Accountability, ensuring that executive privilege is legally pierced regarding the Jeffrey Epstein cover-up, and that the physical intimidation of elected officials is met with the full defensive force of Article I of the Constitution.”

Committee Jurisdictions

Jurisdiction Directive I (The Investigative Front):
The factual specifications regarding the concealment of the Jeffrey Epstein files and the subsequent contempt of Congress shall be managed under the direction of Rep. Robert Garcia via the House Oversight Committee, working in tandem with Vice Ranking Member Becca Balint on the House Judiciary Committee to fast-track the articles. The statutory violations regarding unauthorized conflicts and the flouting of the Leahy Law shall be litigated by Rep. Sara Jacobs and Rep. Yassamin Ansari through the Committees on Foreign Affairs and Armed Services, ensuring that the evidence gathered from the Hegseth inquiry is fully integrated into the omnibus impeachment case against the President.

Senate Enforcement Protocol

🏛️The 2027 Senate Impeachment Trial shall be managed by Majority Leader Chuck Schumer to eliminate executive stonewalling. By utilizing an unprecedented "Juror-Witness" framework, the prosecution shall call Senators Kim, Padilla, Kelly, and Slotkin to give direct, firsthand testimony of physical and digital executive assaults, rendering the administration's defensive claims of standard administrative privilege legally void on the Senate floor.

I hope my articles of impeachment support Democratic lawmakers' cases in framing President Trump for his wrongdoings in the United States during his second presidency (2025–present), including immigration crackdown by ICE, the Epstein case, and unauthorized acts of war. I also hope Democrats visit this blog post to support my case against President Trump, especially if they plan to bring my articles of impeachment to the House floor in Washington, D.C., after the 2026 midterm elections.

Note to all people living in the United States of America:

  • If you currently live here, whether you are a natural-born or a naturalized citizen, then you are protected under the 14th Amendment in terms of Equal Protection rights.
  • If an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent or two stop by at your house in your neighborhood, DO NOT open the door for them! They have no reason to enter your house property to detain or deport you without a judicial warrant. You have a right to question those federal agents or remain silent while your own house door is closed and locked to prevent their entry without your permission.
  • In case you are encountered by an ICE/CBP agent in a public municipality, I highly recommend you to have a state ID, driver's license, or passport to show proof of your citizenship.

item.title: Reproductive Freedom Amendment (RFA)
item.dc:creator: allenacnguyen
item.content:encoded:
I, Allen Nguyen — an independent citizen from Houston, TX, and a Summa Cum Laude graduate from the University of Houston with a Bachelor of Science in Digital Media degree — introduce a constitutional amendment that would legalize abortion at all states at all stages of pregnancy. I would also include a clause that the right to abortion is absolute prior to fetal viability, while allowing state to regulate or limit abortion only after fetal viability with an exception to save a pregnant person by the professional judgment of a licensed physician or a healthcare practitioner.

Amendment Slogan

"Our Bodies. Our Privacy. Our Freedom."

UPDATE 6/26/2026: Reworked constitutional language.

Reproductive Freedom Amendment

Section 1: Fundamental Right to Reproductive Healthcare

Section 1. The right of all persons to reproductive freedom — including the right to obtain and access abortion, contraception, fertility treatment (including in vitro fertilization), miscarriage care, prenatal care, childbirth care, and other reproductive healthcare services — shall not be denied, abridged, or infringed by the United States or by any State on account of sex, pregnancy, reproductive status, or the exercise of bodily autonomy.

The exercise of rights protected under this article shall not be restricted, denied, or penalized within any public benefits program, publicly funded healthcare system, or private health insurance plan, nor shall any person be denied emergency care based on institutional or corporate policy.

Subject only to the post-viability provisions set forth in Section 2, the right to reproductive freedom as defined in this Section shall be absolute, and any law, rule, or policy that prohibits, denies, or penalizes its exercise shall be void ab initio. Any administrative, licensing, or facility regulation that indirectly touches upon, delays, or burdens the availability of services protected under this article shall be subject to strict scrutiny upon judicial review, where the defending party must demonstrate a compelling interest achieved through the absolute least restrictive means possible. The protections guaranteed against discrimination and denial of care under this article shall be absolute, and the rights herein shall not be balanced against, diminished by, or subject to exemptions under any federal or state statute, including laws protecting religious, moral, or conscientious objections of corporate, institutional, or employer entities.

Section 2: Fetal Viability Regulation Clause

Section 2. The right to abortion shall be absolute prior to fetal viability, which shall be determined solely by the good-faith professional judgment of the attending licensed healthcare practitioner based on the specific medical facts of the pregnancy. No State shall enact statutory definitions, diagnostic mandates, or evidentiary standards to restrict or influence the practitioner's viability determination, nor shall the designation of 'qualified healthcare practitioner' be narrowed from its standard clinical definition to restrict the scope of available providers. Neither the United States nor any State shall prohibit, impose an undue burden upon, or otherwise interfere with the exercise of such right prior to fetal viability.

After fetal viability, a State may regulate or limit abortion; provided that no law or regulation shall prohibit an abortion when, in the professional judgment of a licensed physician or other qualified healthcare practitioner, the abortion is necessary to preserve the life, physical health, severe and debilitating mental health conditions diagnosed by a qualified licensed professional, or bodily integrity, including conditions that may become life-threatening or cause severe, long-term health complications if treatment is delayed, of the pregnant person.

Physicians and other qualified healthcare practitioners facilitating or dispensing care under this Section shall possess absolute immunity from criminal prosecution, civil liability, or administrative retribution, including the suspension or revocation of professional licensing, by any State or political subdivision.

No State shall impose targeted regulatory, licensing, licensing fees, insurance mandates, or administrative requirements on reproductive healthcare providers, facilities, or patients that are more stringent than those imposed on other outpatient medical practices of similar clinical risk. No State shall modify professional licensing, certification, or scope-of-practice standards; nor shall any State manipulate, delay, artificially backlog, or withhold the administrative processing of professional licenses, institutional certifications, or residency approvals; for the purpose of penalizing, restricting, or discouraging any healthcare practitioner from providing or assisting in care protected under this article.

Section 3: Travel, Distribution, & Interstate Commerce Shield Clause

Section 3. Neither the United States nor any State shall penalize, prosecute, investigate, detain, extradite, or otherwise impose liability upon any person for traveling across State lines, assisting another person in traveling across State lines, or providing, prescribing, dispensing, manufacturing, or distributing lawful reproductive healthcare services by mail, common carrier, telehealth, interactive computer services, or any other means of interstate commerce. Notwithstanding the Extradition Clause of Article IV, Section 2 of this Constitution, no State shall extradite, nor shall the United States compel the extradition of, any person for conduct or travel protected under this article. Full faith and credit shall not be given to any civil or criminal judgment arising from conduct protected under this article.

Section 4: Enhanced Shield, Data Privacy, & Distribution Protection Clause

Section 4. The privacy of all persons in matters concerning reproductive healthcare shall be protected. Neither the United States nor any State shall compel the disclosure, collection, sale, transfer, or use of personal medical, digital, biometric, geolocation, communication, or reproductive health data; nor utilize artificial intelligence, machine learning, or automatic algorithmic systems to infer, predict, or synthesize such data; for the purpose of investigating, penalizing, or restricting the exercise of rights protected by this article. Any data or algorithmic inferences obtained or transferred in violation of this Section, whether voluntarily surrendered or compelled, shall be inadmissible in any criminal, civil, or administrative proceeding. No person, healthcare provider, telecommunications provider, technology company, data broker, or other private actor shall be compelled to participate in the enforcement of laws inconsistent with this article.

No prior or existing federal or state statute, including but not limited to laws regulating the postal service or common carriers, shall be construed or enforced to restrict, prohibit, or penalize the mailing, shipping, or transportation of medications, equipment, medical instruments, devices, information, or supplies used for reproductive healthcare services protected under this article.

Section 5: Enforcement Clause

Section 5. Congress shall have the absolute power to enforce and implement this article by appropriate legislation, including the power to prevent any State or private actor from imposing any burden, restriction, or penalty on the rights protected herein.

Section 6: Immediate Effect Clause

Section 6. This article of amendment shall take effect immediately upon ratification by three-fourths of the States. This article shall be entirely self-executing, immediately operative upon ratification, and judicially enforceable without the prerequisite of enabling legislation; and the absence of congressional enforcement legislation shall not be construed to delay, restrict, or deny the immediate judicial enforcement of any right guaranteed herein; notwithstanding any prior statute, executive order, or common-law doctrine to the contrary.

Legal & technical breakdown

Section 1: Fundamental Right to Reproductive Healthcare

Constitutional Purpose: Establishes an un-waivable, comprehensive right to the full spectrum of reproductive care.

Intended Outcome: Subjects any restrictive state policy to strict scrutiny, shifts the burden of proof to the state, and eliminates religious, moral, or corporate exemptions to ensure uniform healthcare access.

Section 2: Fetal Viability Regulation Clause

Constitutional Purpose: Protects the pre-viability right to abortion and outlaws targeted administrative attacks on providers.

Intended Outcome: Leaves the determination of viability solely to clinical practitioners, grants absolute civil and criminal immunity to medical staff, and outlaws artificial administrative backlogs or discriminatory medical licensing practices.

Section 3: Travel, Distribution, & Interstate Commerce Shield Clause

Constitutional Purpose: Secures interstate pathways for reproductive medicine and travel.

Intended Outcomes: Prevents hostile states from criminalizing or investigating cross-border travel for healthcare, protects mail-order medication distribution, and bars courts from enforcing out-of-state anti-abortion judgments.

Section 4: Enhanced Shield, Data Privacy, & Distribution Protection Clause

Constitutional Purpose: Insulates personal digital footprints from being weaponized by law enforcement.

Intended Outcomes: Bans the forced collection or sale of reproductive geolocation and communication metadata, shields private tech companies from enforcing restrictive state laws, and overrides legacy postal statutes.

Section 5: Enforcement Clause

Constitutional Purpose: Empowers federal legislative intervention.

Intended Outcome: Grants Congress explicit, sweeping authority to pass civil rights legislation to actively dismantle state or private interference with reproductive freedom.

Section 6: Immediate Effect Clause

Constitutional Purpose: Enacts immediate legal authority.

Intended Outcome: Declares the amendment self-executing upon ratification, ensuring it is instantly judicially enforceable by citizens without requiring Congress to pass enabling laws first.

Overall Constitutional Purpose (Absolute Bodily Sovereignty)

The RFA operates under the philosophy that bodily integrity is a pre-political, foundational right that cannot be negotiated, diluted, or balanced away by legislative majorities. By shifting the burden of proof entirely to the state under strict scrutiny and declaring restrictions void ab initio (void from the beginning), it establishes bodily autonomy as an absolute constitutional wall.

Underlying Philosophy (Anti-Surveillance & Healthcare Equity)

It recognizes that in the 21st century, bodily freedom is inextricably linked to data sovereignty. The amendment treats reproductive choices not merely as a private moral decision, but as a critical node of digital and civil data that must be insulated from corporate data brokers and the overreach of local law enforcement networks.

Societal Goals

  • Establishment of Data Sanctuaries: Permanently shielding personal healthcare, biometric, and geolocation data from cross-border legal weaponization.
  • Eradication of Healthcare Deserts: Eliminating discriminatory state administrative and licensing barriers (TRAP laws) to ensure regular medical access in historically underserved regions.
  • Absolute Practitioner Security: Guaranteeing total civil, criminal, and professional immunity for medical professionals to preserve the integrity of the patient-provider relationship.
  • Equal Access to Care: Ensuring that public benefit programs, public networks, and private insurers cannot leverage economic status to deny or restrict reproductive health services.
  • —
  • Individual Rights
    • Protect bodily autonomy and reproductive decision-making.
    • Guarantee access to reproductive healthcare regardless of state of residence.
    • Reduce legal uncertainty surrounding abortion rights.
    • Protect individuals from prosecution for exercising constitutionally protected reproductive rights.
  • Healthcare Access
    • Protect physicians, pharmacists, nurses, and other healthcare practitioners providing protected care.
    • Support access to abortion medication, telehealth services, and reproductive-health services.
    • Preserve access to reproductive healthcare in states that would otherwise restrict it.
  • Interstate Mobility
    • Protect travel across state lines for reproductive healthcare.
    • Protect those assisting others in obtaining reproductive healthcare.
    • Prevent states from extending abortion restrictions beyond their own borders.
  • Privacy and Technology
    • Protect medical privacy and reproductive-health information.
    • Restrict government use of digital, geolocation, communication, and health data for reproductive-health investigations.
    • Limit the use of technology and surveillance systems to enforce abortion restrictions.
  • Distribution and Infrastructure
    • Protect interstate shipment and delivery of reproductive-health medications and supplies.
    • Protect pharmacies, telehealth providers, manufacturers, distributors, delivery services, and common carriers involved in protected reproductive healthcare.
    • Ensure that healthcare infrastructure cannot be indirectly targeted to undermine constitutional rights.
  • Federal-State Regulations
    • Override conflicting state abortion bans and restrictions.
    • Establish a nationwide constitutional baseline for reproductive rights.
    • Reduce interstate legal conflicts involving reproductive healthcare.

Exhibits leading to this amendment proposal

  • 📉 Exhibit A: Maternal Mortality and Severe Gestational Complications
  • 🏥 Exhibit B: Institutional Collapse and the Closure of Clinical Facilities
  • ⚖️ Exhibit C: Criminalization and Prosecutorial Terror Targeting Pregnant People
  • 🧑‍⚕️ Exhibit D: The Legal Chilling Effect on Healthcare Practitioners
  • 📱 Exhibit E: Cross-Border Digital Surveillance and Data Weaponization
  • 📦 Exhibit F: Supply Chain Disruption and Medication Interdiction

📉 Exhibit A: Maternal Mortality and Severe Gestational Complications

Following the Dobbs decision, states implementing near-total abortion restrictions triggered an immediate healthcare crisis. Vague statutory language regarding exceptions has forced clinicians to delay life-saving stabilizing care, driving a measurable rise in preventable maternal morbidity.

  • The Data Baseline: Peer-reviewed public health studies published in the American Journal of Public Health tracked a 9.2% increase in pregnancy-associated deaths across 14 states that enacted total or six-week abortion restrictions immediately post-Dobbs. This translated to dozens of excess, preventable deaths within the first 18 months alone.
    —
  • The Texas Spike: In Texas, the impact of compounding restrictions led to a staggering 56% increase in maternal mortality between 2019 and 2022, vastly outstripping a modest 11% national increase recorded over the exact same time frame.

Amendment Intent: Exhibit A

The RFA establishes a supreme constitutional guarantee of bodily autonomy under Section 1 (Fundamental Right to Reproductive Healthcare), stripping state legislatures of the power to pass piecemeal restrictions that interfere with immediate, medical interventions.
