Exhibits leading to this amendment proposal

  • 🚙 Exhibit A: The Multi-State Rental Car Loophole
  • 🚨 Exhibit B: The High-Impact Rollover Emergency
  • 🩺 Exhibit C: The Algorithmic Healthcare Prior-Authorization Denial
  • 🪪 Exhibit D: The Deepfake Social-Engineering Banking Fraud
  • 🪙 Exhibit E: The Immutable Blockchain Ledger Drain
  • 📞 Exhibit F: The Spoofed Local-Area Insurance Robocall
  • 🤰 Exhibit G: The Post-Dobbs Obstetric Emergency and Insurance Care Delays
  • 🛠️ Exhibit H: The Punitive Striking Worker Benefit Expiry
  • ⚖️ Exhibit I: The New Hampshire Financial Responsibility Outlier

🏛️ Part I: Possible Insurance & Loophole Cases

🚙 Exhibit A: The Multi-State Rental Car Loophole

During cross-border interstate transit, drivers and families frequently face a fractured legal landscape where individual states maintain wildly inconsistent financial responsibility thresholds or allow drivers to completely opt out of compulsory coverage. When collisions occur involving out-of-state rental agreements and municipal property damage, corporate insurance syndicates exploit these geographical boundaries, using automated digital platforms to delay claims and trap traveling families in jurisdictional limbo.

  • The Interstate Rental Intersection Dispute: In August 2025, a family traveling from Texas to a wedding in the Philadelphia area is involved in a multi-state roadway collision. While driving a silver Chrysler minivan rented from the Alamo fleet at the Philadelphia International Airport (PHL) hub, the driver proceeds straight through a New Jersey road intersection with the absolute right-of-way under a green light and at a proper, legal speed. An oncoming white sedan executes an illegal left turn, directly obstructing the straight path. The driver of the minivan attempts to brake immediately, but the momentum results in a front-bumper collision against the right side of the obstructing white sedan. The force of the impact deflects the sedan, causing it to collide with an adjacent brown utility pole.
    —
  • The Scene Safety and Law Enforcement Response: A passenger in the vehicle immediately activates the emergency flashers, providing a vital visual warning to trailing traffic and successfully preventing dangerous secondary rear-end accidents at the busy junction. Upon the arrival of a responding law enforcement officer, the passenger responsibly communicates the unexpected nature of the event to the officer before stepping back to allow the official, human-led exchange of driver’s licenses and insurance information to proceed between the parties. Although the impacted brown utility pole remains completely standing and structurally intact, the local municipality, the third-party insurer, and the rental corporation may launch competing claims behind the scenes. Rather than assigning human investigators, the insurance carriers may deploy algorithmic claim-scrubbing software that flags the cross-border rental contract and vehicle layout, generating an automated "coverage hold" that threatens to hold the non-at-fault family personally liable for the infrastructure incident and vehicle exchange logistics.

Intent of the Amendment: Exhibit A

The IFSA standardizes the laws of the road to protect citizens from interstate corporate exploitation. Section 5 establishes an unalterable, uniform federal mandate for automobile financial responsibility that applies equally across all fifty states, rendering state-level optional insurance loopholes entirely null and void. By enforcing a single national baseline, the amendment guarantees that cross-border rental liabilities and third-party property damages are processed under identical legal standards, while Section 4 prohibits insurance syndicates from utilizing automated black-box algorithms to freeze or deny coverage to families traveling away from home.

🔍 System Breakdown: Standardizing Cross-Border Roadway Protection

  • Dismantling State Financial Anomalies: Currently, fractured state-by-state laws allow regional exemptions — such as New Hampshire's optional insurance framework — which leave out-of-state motorists highly vulnerable to uninsured drivers. Section 5 wipes out these regional loopholes by making valid liability and comprehensive coverage an ironclad federal prerequisite for operating any motor vehicle on a public road anywhere in the United States.
    —
  • Eliminating Algorithmic Claim Freezes: To protect corporate profit margins after multi-vehicle collisions, insurance companies rely on automated screening programs that flag out-of-state rental agreements to artificially delay payouts. Section 4 enforces a strict human-review requirement, stripping corporations of the power to let software automatically stall a traveling family's claim processing or retroactively penalize a responsible vehicle exchange.
    —
  • Simplifying Municipal Property Restitution: Because city public works departments routinely issue steep invoices for structural integrity inspections and superficial repairs after an asset is struck — even when a utility pole remains standing and intact — Section 5 locks a uniform property damage liability minimum into every active policy nationwide. This ensures these administrative municipal costs are absorbed automatically by the insurance pool, preventing innocent, right-of-way drivers from being personally billed by local governments.

🚨 Exhibit B: The High-Impact Rollover Emergency

In high-stakes, severe traffic accidents involving catastrophic vehicle damage and rollover dynamics, victims face immediate financial and administrative vulnerability. While emergency services focus on active rescue and clearing blocked intersections, insurance cartels capitalize on the immediate trauma and chaos of the aftermath, utilizing predictive AI algorithms and automated photo-scanning software to shortchange vehicle values, rush lowball settlements, and evade their structural obligations to injured citizens.

  • The West Houston Intersection Rollover: A driver operating a compact SUV is struck at a high-velocity metropolitan intersection (such as Bellaire Blvd and Corporate Dr), causing the vehicle to completely overturn upside down, shatter its front windshield, and deploy all primary airbags. The catastrophic crash triggers an immediate, multi-agency emergency response — including three police units, a fire truck, an ambulance, and multiple heavy-duty tow trucks — who work to extricate the occupants and clear the wreckage to a nearby commercial banking parking lot.
    —
  • The On-Scene Fault Clearance and Corporate Backlash: Although the responding police officers on the scene utilize eyewitness testimony to explicitly clear the rolled-over driver of any fault, the driver's family is instantly hit with thousands of dollars in emergency service bills, paramedic fees, and towing charges. When the total-loss claim is submitted, the opposing carrier uses an automated valuation algorithm that looks at digital photos of the upside-down wreckage to automatically reduce the vehicle's cash payout by 40%, attempting to force the traumatized victim into an immediate, binding digital settlement before medical evaluations are completed.

Intent of the Amendment: Exhibit B

The IFSA acts as an ironclad financial shield during moments of severe physical trauma. Section 5 mandates that every driver sharing the public pavement must maintain verified insurance or approved security, guaranteeing that non-at-fault victims of catastrophic crashes have immediate access to a secure, federalized recovery pool for vehicle replacement and medical emergency bills. Simultaneously, Section 4 outlaws the weaponization of automated underwriting and algorithmic total-loss depreciations, ensuring that a qualified human adjuster must personally review police reports and handle the claim with dignity.

🔍 System Breakdown: Securing Emergency Trauma Recovery

  • An Absolute Guardrail Against AI Lowballing: In the wake of severe rollover crashes, modern insurance companies use predictive AI to scan photos of the vehicle damage and instantly calculate the lowest possible settlement the victim might accept out of desperation. Section 4 establishes an absolute constitutional barrier against this practice, ensuring that an automated system can never issue an unreviewed vehicle valuation or deny a total-loss claim.
    —
  • Guaranteed Emergency Pool Access: High-impact collisions require massive municipal deployment (firefighters, paramedics, multiple tow fleets) that generate immediate, overlapping bills. Because Section 5 enforces a strict, uniform federal mandate for all drivers, it guarantees that a valid, verified policy is always active on the scene to cover these emergency response costs, preventing a non-at-fault driver's credit or savings from being destroyed by emergency service invoices.
    —
  • The Primacy of Human Fact-Finding: When an accident results in a rolled-over vehicle, corporate lawyers frequently use digital tracking data or arbitrary shift metrics to twist the narrative of the crash. Section 4 forces the legal process to rely strictly on human-verified facts — such as the on-scene determinations made by responding police officers and the testimonies of family witnesses — ensuring corporate algorithms cannot override real human evidence.

🩺 Exhibit C: The Algorithmic Healthcare Prior-Authorization Denial

In the modern corporate medical landscape, major healthcare insurers have consolidated massive control by automating their utilization review systems. Rather than employing physicians to carefully review complex patient charts, corporate insurance syndicates utilize black-box AI algorithms to process thousands of insurance claims simultaneously, issuing sweeping automated denials for critical post-acute care and medical therapies to protect corporate profit margins.

  • The Automated Care Ceiling: A senior patient recovering from an aggressive orthopedic surgery or cardiac event is transferred to a post-acute rehabilitation facility. While the treating facility physician explicitly documents that the patient requires a minimum of three weeks of intensive physical therapy to safely regain mobility, the health insurance provider routing the claim utilizes a predictive AI model (such as UnitedHealth’s controversial nH Predict platform).
    —
  • The Human-In-The-Loop Illusion: The algorithmic software calculates a standardized, statistical recovery baseline based on arbitrary group metrics, completely ignoring the patient’s individual medical history. Within seconds, the software automatically issues an adverse coverage determination—denying the remainder of the skilled nursing stay—and forces the medical facility to discharge the patient prematurely or stick the family with thousands of dollars in un-reimbursed medical debt.

Intent of the Amendment: Exhibit C

The IFSA establishes human sovereignty over life-saving health decisions. Section 4 imposes an absolute constitutional prohibition against automated, machine-driven denials of health insurance benefits and prior-authorization requests. By explicitly stipulating that no adverse insurance determination can be finalized without a comprehensive, independent evaluation by a qualified medical peer, the amendment permanently strips healthcare corporations of the power to let algorithmic models override the physical determinations of treating physicians.

🔍 System Breakdown: Dismantling Healthcare AI Gatekeeping

  • The Eradication of Statistical Underwriting: Modern healthcare cartels rely on automated care-support software to group patients into generic recovery curves, treating human bodies like algorithms. Section 4 forces all health insurers to base medical necessity determinations entirely on the unique clinical history and real-world circumstances of the specific enrollee.
    —
  • Enforcing the Primacy of Licensed Peers: To cut administrative overhead, insurance companies use non-clinical staff to sign off on automated computer rejections. The IFSA structurally mandates that any reduction, delay, or denial of a requested health benefit must be reviewed and authorized solely by a licensed clinical peer competent in that specific medical field.
    —
  • Preventing Irreparable Discharge Injury: When an algorithm abruptly cuts off rehabilitation coverage, families are forced to navigate a exhausting multi-tiered corporate appeal process while care is actively paused. Section 4–2 establishes that the filing of a medical dispute automatically freezes the status quo, forcing the insurer to continue funding the patient’s active clinical care throughout the entire human-led review window.

🪪 Exhibit D: The Deepfake Social-Engineering Banking Fraud

The rapid industrialization of consumer-facing financial technology has created a massive spike in synthetic identity theft and advanced social engineering scams. Financial institutions heavily utilize automated transaction-monitoring AI to guard against liability, often weaponizing these exact same algorithms against everyday consumers by instantly denying fraud-recovery claims under the pretext that the victim "authorized" the transaction via a compromised password or security link.

  • The Voice-Cloned Smishing Campaign: An everyday consumer receives an urgent SMS notification masquerading as a routine road-toll platform or utility notification (such as the widespread E-ZPass smishing networks orchestrated by illicit Telegram syndicates). When the consumer attempts to verify the text, they are targeted by a sophisticated social engineering scheme utilizing an AI-generated synthetic voice clone of a banking fraud investigator.
    —
  • The Automated Fraud Lockout: The caller convinces the victim to move liquid assets to a "secure safety vault" via a standard digital transfer. Once the consumer realizes they have been defrauded and files an emergency dispute, the bank's automated fraud-scrubbing software flags that the user inputted their own credentials, triggers an automated "claim closed" status, and refuses to issue a reimbursement, leaving the citizen completely financially ruined with zero recourse.

Intent of the Amendment: Exhibit D

The IFSA protects the financial sovereignty of citizens caught in the crosshairs of industrialized digital crime. Section 4 guarantees consumer protection by establishing a constitutional right to human-managed fraud investigations. It bars banking institutions from using automated scripts to instantly dismiss fraud disputes, while empowering Congress to set uniform claims-handling standards that force multi-billion-dollar financial platforms to carry robust consumer-fraud insurance pools to buffer everyday citizens from AI-driven social engineering.

🔍 System Breakdown: Equalizing the Consumer-Banking Power Dynamic

  • Banning the "Credential Loophole" Dismissal: Under current financial frameworks, banks systematically escape liability for wire fraud if the consumer was coerced into hitting "submit" themselves. Section 4 outlaws the use of automated algorithms that look purely at technical log-in data to dismiss a claim, forcing a human investigator to examine the presence of deceptive, external criminal influence.
    —
  • Mandating Institutional Risk Buffers: Because sophisticated cybercriminal organizations operate with industrialized phishing-as-a-service infrastructure, the individual consumer cannot reasonably out-defend them alone. The structural mandates within the IFSA provide the legal mechanism to force financial networks to maintain systemic consumer-reimbursement reserves, treating fraud losses as a cost of institutional operations rather than personal ruin.
    —
  • Securing Transparent Forensic Audits: When a fraud dispute is processed today, banks hide behind proprietary, opaque security metrics to deny claims without explanation. Section 4–3 forces financial networks to hand over comprehensive, human-readable documentation regarding how the transaction was processed, giving the consumer a fair legal standing to contest the bank's internal conclusions.

🪙 Exhibit E: The Immutable Blockchain Ledger Drain

Cryptocurrency and decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms are structurally engineered around the principle of code-enforced immutability. Because blockchain networks rely on distributed cryptographic ledgers, any transaction—once validated by the network—is fundamentally and technically irreversible. Exploiting this absolute permanence, malicious actors utilize automated malicious smart contracts, wallet drainers, and high-yield investment "pig butchering" scams to permanently strip users of their digital savings without any structural safety net.

  • The Automated Wallet-Drainer Trap: A digital media asset manager or retail investor interacts with a decentralized web interface that has been compromised by a malicious script (such as an Inferno Drainer framework). Believing they are approving a routine data-verification signature, the user clicks "confirm" on their hardware wallet browser extension.
    —
  • The Permanent Asset Liquidation: The malicious smart contract instantly executes, reading the user’s private keys to drain the entire decentralized wallet liquidity pool within 70 seconds. Because the assets are routed through automated cross-chain bridges and decentralized exchanges (DEXs) to un-hosted wallets, the consumer has no centralized server to appeal to, no "cancel transaction" button to press, and no automatic corporate insurance to trigger a recovery.

Intent of the Amendment: Exhibit E

While no law can alter the mathematics of blockchain physics or mechanically "undo" an immutable cryptographic block, the IFSA elegantly reshapes the financial safety nets surrounding digital asset custody. Section 4 mandates that any commercial entity or digital exchange operating within the United States financial system must provide strict, human-led dispute mechanisms and carry systemic, regulated risk and consumer-fraud insurance backstops to insulate users from catastrophic digital asset drainage.

🔍 System Breakdown: Governing the Unregulated Digital Frontier

  • Forcing Insured Fiat-to-Crypto Boundaries: The greatest point of exposure for consumers occurs at the boundary where traditional cash converts into digital tokens. The IFSA requires all federally regulated crypto exchanges (such as Blockchain, Coinbase, or Kraken) to maintain ironclad consumer asset insurance, guaranteeing cash-equivalent replacement value to users defrauded via web-interface security lapses.
    —
  • Capping Algorithmic Disclaimers: Decentralized platforms routinely mask predatory losses behind automated "at-your-own-risk" terms of service written directly into code. Section 4 effectively outlaws these automated legal waivers, establishing that no digital financial service can bypass federal consumer protection baselines simply by operating via decentralized smart contracts.
    —
  • Establishing Coordinated Human-Led Recovery Protocols: Because tracking stolen digital assets requires rapid, manual on-chain and off-chain intelligence gathering, Section 4 forces financial institutions to provide immediate access to a human cyber-fraud specialist upon a breach report. This replaces automated chatbot loops with professional human investigators who can coordinate with law enforcement to flag and freeze illicit exit-ramps before the stolen currency is laundered permanently.

📞 Exhibit F: The Spoofed Local-Area Insurance Robocall

Illicit lead-generation cartels and predatory telecom brokers weaponize automated algorithmic dialers to saturate public cellular networks with deceptive, high-volume robocalls. By manipulating Caller ID metadata to spoof local geographic area codes and deploying hyper-realistic interactive voice software, these networks bypass traditional consumer filters, leaving deceptive voicemails to harvest sensitive data or trap consumers in non-compliant insurance schemes.

  • The Neighborhood Spoofing and Voicemail Bait: A citizen is targeted multiple times, receiving between two to four incoming calls per weekday displaying their exact local area code (such as Houston's 713 or 281). When the consumer utilizes active smartphone filtering to silence the unknown number, the automated dialer hits the voicemail box and plays a highly calculated, pre-recorded interactive voice script: "Hello? Uh, can you hear me?" complete with engineered human pauses and verbal tics designed to mimic a live, struggling caller.
    —
  • The Data-Harvesting and Junk-Enrollment Trap: The primary goal of this deceptive speech-bot is to trick the recipient into answering or responding to log the phone number as a "verified active line" in a premium cyber-fraud registry. If a consumer falls for the ruse and engages, the network routes them to an aggressive offshore broker who uses high-pressure scripts to harvest their date of birth, social security data, or bank routing numbers under the guise of "verifying Obamacare eligibility," ultimately executing a fraudulent "silent enrollment" that switches their actual health insurance to a junk plan without their consent.

Intent of the Amendment: Exhibit F

The IFSA establishes an absolute constitutional barrier against the predatory exploitation of the insurance market. Section 4 explicitly outlaws the use of automated, unverified algorithmic systems to market, solicit, or enroll citizens in financial and insurance products. It strips deceptive lead-generation cartels of the ability to hide behind automated spoofing networks, mandating that all insurance solicitations maintain a transparent, human-verified chain of custody and granting consumers a direct constitutional cause of action to penalize platforms that facilitate predatory, automated financial harassment.

🔍 System Breakdown: Eradicating Automated Insurance Harassment

  • Criminalizing Algorithmic Speech-Bots: Current telemarketing laws impose minor civil fines that large corporate lead-generators treat as a simple cost of doing business. Section 4 establishes that using automated voice synthesis or algorithmic dialing systems to solicit insurance products—including deceptive conversational baits left in voicemail boxes—constitutes an explicit violation of consumer financial security, forcing telecom carriers to permanently drop traffic from unverified automated brokers.
    —
  • Enforcing a Human-Verified Traceability Standard: To bypass smartphone filters, predatory actors rapidly cycle through thousands of fake, spoofed local numbers. The structural provisions of the IFSA mandate an ironclad, human-verified authentication protocol for any entity claiming to represent a licensed insurance company or government health program, allowing networks to instantly block unauthenticated spoofed traffic before it reaches a citizen's device.
    —
  • Nullifying Unauthorized Plan Switching: Illicit brokers routinely use harvested personal data to execute "silent enrollments," switching a citizen's official healthcare plan on public exchanges without their knowledge. Section 4 implements a strict "human consent firewall," declaring any insurance policy change or enrollment executed via automated robocall solicitation or deceptive lead harvesting to be legally void from its inception.

🤰 Exhibit G: The Post-Dobbs Obstetric Emergency and Insurance Care Delays

Following the fragmentation of reproductive healthcare laws across individual states, pregnant patients experiencing sudden, severe labor or gestational complications face a dual crisis: restrictive state statutory penalties and predatory insurance gatekeeping. Insurance cartels and hospital risk-management syndicates utilize automated liability-screening protocols to delay or deny coverage for standard, life-saving obstetric interventions (such as emergency terminations or surgical evacuations), leaving patients in active physical trauma while navigating localized legal chaos.

  • The Conflicting Jurisdictional Medical Crisis: A pregnant patient experiencing a sudden premature rupture of membranes or severe preeclampsia at 19 weeks enters a major metropolitan emergency room. While the attending obstetricians determine that the fetus is non-viable and the patient is rapidly developing a life-threatening uterine infection (sepsis), the hospital's legal department and the third-party health insurance provider intervene to freeze the care plan.
    —
  • The Algorithmic Liability Stall: Fearing ambiguous state-level criminal liabilities and statutory fines, the insurer's automated utilization review system flags the requested emergency intervention as an "unauthorized termination procedure." The platform automatically generates a coverage denial or administrative hold, forcing doctors to delay critical care and wait until the patient deteriorates to the absolute brink of organ failure before human adjusters approve the mandatory medical treatment.

Intent of the Amendment: Exhibit G

The IFSA secures the physical and financial survival of citizens facing acute medical trauma. Section 4 establishes an absolute constitutional firewall that outlaws the use of automated algorithms or corporate risk-screening software to delay, reduce, or deny emergency medical coverage for pregnant patients in labor or crisis. Working in perfect tandem with the RFA (Reproductive Freedom Amendment), the IFSA mandates that any emergency medical determination made by an on-scene, treating physician must be funded immediately and unconditionally by the insurance carrier, stripping corporate entities of the power to weaponize localized statutory confusion against human life.

🔍 System Breakdown: Enforcing Immediate Care in Maternal Trauma

  • Dismantling Corporate Liability Shields: Under current post-Dobbs legal frameworks, insurance platforms exploit ambiguous state laws to delay care, shifting the physical risk entirely onto the patient. Section 4 strips these platforms of their gatekeeping power by establishing that the economic and medical necessity decisions of the on-scene treating physician override all automated corporate policies.
    —
  • Banning the "Abortion Penalty" Flag: Insurance underwriting systems use automated keywords to automatically flag and stall coverage for complex pregnancy terminations, even when medically required to prevent maternal mortality. The IFSA outlaws these automated billing blocks, ensuring that all obstetric procedures, emergency labor operations, and therapeutic interventions are processed under a uniform, national consumer-protection baseline.
    —
  • Immediate Financial Immunization for Providers: To prevent hospitals from delaying life-saving labor care out of fear of financial ruin or insurance clawbacks, the IFSA guarantees a federally backed, instant-payment mandate for all emergency stabilizing care. This ensures that doctors can focus entirely on executing their medical oaths and saving the patient's life, free from the threat of retroactive corporate financial penalties.

🛠️ Exhibit H: The Punitive Striking Worker Benefit Expiry

During organized labor disputes, private corporate syndicates and hostile public sector employers weaponize the administrative control of health insurance and retirement benefits as tools of economic coercion. Exploiting punitive state statutes designed to strip public employees of their hard-earned pensions and seniority, management utilizes automated human resource platforms to instantly terminate healthcare coverage upon the initiation of a strike, forcing workers and their families into severe medical vulnerability to break collective bargaining leverage.

  • The Statutory Public Sector Asset Stripping: Public sector workers (such as municipal transit operators or public educators) executing a targeted work stoppage face severe retaliation under punitive state laws (such as Texas Government Code § 617.003 or Florida Statute § 447.505). These statutes mandate the immediate forfeiture of the workers' accumulated pensions, accrued seniority, and state-backed health insurance, treating an active labor dispute as a total abandonment of employment.
    —
  • The Automated Benefit Lockout: Concurrently, in both the public and private sectors, management deploys automated HR algorithms that monitor digital clock-in data. The moment a strike threshold is crossed, the software automatically triggers a mass-cancellation of health insurance policies, cutting off coverage for ongoing medical therapies, prescription drugs, and labor-delivery services for the striking workers’ families to force a concession before contract negotiations even begin.

Intent of the Amendment: Exhibit H

The IFSA establishes that earned health and financial benefits are an unalterable right of labor, not a weapon of corporate or state warfare. Section 4 imposes an absolute constitutional barrier against the retroactive, punitive, or automated cancellation of health insurance plans, pensions, and accrued benefits during a declared labor dispute. Acting in complete alignment with the LSA (Labor Stoppage Amendment), the IFSA guarantees that workers in both the public and private sectors can exercise their right to strike without facing immediate medical or retirement ruin, forcing employers to negotiate on the human merits of the contract rather than relying on algorithmic starvation tactics.

🔍 System Breakdown: Insulating Worker Benefits from Striking Retaliation

  • Dismantling State Penalty Statutes: Punitive state laws explicitly target the financial security of public servants by stripping them of their retirement pools and health benefits if they picket. The IFSA, backed by federal supremacy, completely nullifies provisions like Texas Government Code § 617.003 and Florida Statute § 447.505, rendering any state-sanctioned stripping of pensions or insurance during a labor dispute completely unconstitutional.
    —
  • Banning the "Strike Button" Insurance Cancellation: Employers routinely exploit a loophole that allows them to stop paying insurance premiums the day a strike begins, leaving families one emergency away from financial ruin. Section 4 implements a strict benefit-preservation mandate, requiring that existing healthcare policies remain fully active and undisturbed for a minimum of 90 days during an active labor dispute, with premium balances deferred to the final bargaining resolution.
    —
  • Preventing the Digital Scab Subsidy: To outlast striking workers, employers attempt to divert frozen benefit funds into hiring short-term physical replacements or deploying automated digital scab platforms. The structural mechanics of the IFSA prohibit employers from reallocating the capital reserves of employee benefit funds to finance strikebreaking logistics, ensuring worker-earned capital cannot be weaponized against their own bargaining unit.

⚖️ Exhibit I: The New Hampshire Financial Responsibility Outlier

When motorists cross state lines, they are exposed to highly volatile regional statutory frameworks that completely lack uniform consumer protections. As the lone structural exception in the nation, New Hampshire does not mandate compulsory automobile liability insurance, allowing drivers to operate motor vehicles completely uninsured under a retroactive "financial responsibility" loophole. When collisions occur between out-of-state travelers and uninsured local operators, corporate insurance networks weaponize this statutory anomaly to deploy automated claim-stalling software, delaying critical uninsured motorist coverage payouts to avoid corporate financial outlays.

  • The Uninsured Interstate Collision: A driver or traveling family operating a legally registered vehicle under a standard out-of-state insurance policy or corporate rental agreement enters New Hampshire jurisdiction. While maintaining proper road speed and right-of-way, their vehicle is struck by an uninsured local resident. Because the local operator has opted out of maintaining an active liability policy under the state's unique statutory omission, there is no third-party carrier to absorb the vehicle damage or medical liabilities.
    —
  • The Algorithmic Underinsured Hold: The out-of-state motorist responsibly files an immediate claim under their own policy's Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist (UM/UIM) provision. Rather than deploying an active human adjuster to fast-track recovery capital, the corporate insurer’s automated system flags the unique New Hampshire jurisdictional code. The software automatically places an indefinite administrative hold on the file, forcing the non-at-fault victim to endure multi-month delays while demanding manual, human-compiled legal proof that the striking driver was entirely assetless and uninsured.

Intent of the Amendment: Exhibit I

The IFSA establishes a seamless, unbroken national shield for automobile financial security. Section 5 explicitly strips individual states of the authority to maintain optional or retroactive liability frameworks, mandating that active liability, comprehensive, and uninsured motorist coverage are absolute federal prerequisites for operating any motor vehicle on a public roadway within the United States. By standardizing this requirement nationwide, the IFSA permanently closes the New Hampshire loophole, while Section 4 outlaws the use of automated, black-box processing models that exploit state-level statutory anomalies to stall emergency funds for responsible drivers.

🔍 System Breakdown: Overriding the Retroactive Responsibility Loophole

  • Enforcing a Absolute Federal Prerequisite: The IFSA utilizes federal supremacy to establish a standard baseline for all fifty states, overriding New Hampshire’s retroactive system. By making continuous, verified liability insurance an unalterable requirement to operate any vehicle on a public road, the amendment ensures that no driver can legally expose an interstate traveler to an entirely uninsured asset pool.
    —
  • Eradicating the UM/UIM Verification Delay: Currently, insurance companies exploit the lack of a centralized state insurance database in an optional state to delay payouts, forcing their own customers to prove a negative (that the other driver lacks coverage). Section 4 outlaws these automated verification loops, mandating that once a law enforcement report verifies the opposing vehicle lacks active policy credentials, the victim's carrier must release immediate, human-authorized repair and medical capital within 7 business days.
    —
  • Establishing Direct Institutional Subrogation Pools: Rather than forcing an innocent family to personally navigate the complex legal process of suing an uninsured driver in a foreign state court, Section 5 shifts the entire burden to the institutional level. The victim’s policy pays out immediately, and the insurance carrier is granted an automated federal subrogation right to claw back those funds directly from the at-fault individual’s tax returns or state-level assets, fully insulating the consumer from the financial fallout of the collision.

📊 The IFSA Portfolio Evaluation Matrix

The reason why I introduce this constitutional amendment

I believe insurance should be explicitly mentioned as an importance to protect people from financial loss in unexpected circumstances. Also, for drivers driving a vehicle in the country, since auto insurance is a standard mandate for them in nearly all states (with the exception of New Hampshire that the state doesn't mandate auto insurance), I included a section in this amendment that universally mandates auto insurance regulation in all states (including New Hampshire) to protect drivers from financial loss in the event of vehicle accidents, which will be important for them when they drive.

The purpose of the Insurance and Financial Security Amendment (IFSA) is to explicitly mention insurance as an important aspect of the term for people to be protected from financial loss in any unexpected circumstances.

I also aim to end automated insurance robocalls pretending to be insurance companies and using spoofed phone numbers of the consumers' local area codes.

In this constitutional amendment, I choose not to include the sunset clause, which would give states in the nation a limited amount of time to ratify passed amendments. So, by excluding the sunset clause, I choose to give states flexibility upon passage by Congress on legislative discussions to ratify this constitutional amendment on the explicit mention and importance of insurance.

Constitutional amendments require broad public support and careful national debate. While the Insurance and Financial Security Amendment (IFSA) may be controversial, I welcome constructive comments, criticism, and proposed changes from the public as part of the constitutional process. This is one of my amendment ideas that I believe that all people in the United States should be protected from financial loss or harm with the importance of insurance and have insurance plans and benefits equipped within their own cases.

Steps to take this amendment into law

Once I finalize the draft of this constitutional amendment with some help from other people, legal scholars, or lawmakers by means of review and evaluation, then I would send this amendment article to Washington, D.C., at the U.S. Capitol Hill for Congress to attempt to pass this amendment.

First, under Article V of the United States Constitution in terms of getting the amendment into law, Congress must vote 2/3 in both the House of Representatives and the Senate to pass this constitutional amendment.

  • 290 out of 435 House of Representatives are required to pass
  • 67 out of 100 Senators are required to pass

Alternatively, under Article V of the United States Constitution, a national convention can be called on proposing this constitutional amendment if 2/3 (34 out of 50 states) of state legislatures apply to Congress to do so. This method was never utilized in U.S. history.

Once this constitutional amendment is passed by Congress, then the next step is ratification, which requires at least 3/4 of the states to ratify this constitutional amendment.

  • 38 out of 50 States are required to ratify

If this Insurance and Financial Security Amendment (IFSA) is ratified into the United States Constitution, then it would become the 28th Amendment to the United States Constitution (or 29th Amendment if the Equal Rights Amendment (ERA) is officially ratified and certified first that it was in legal limbo for decades since expiration). This constitutional amendment would explicitly mention insurance as an important aspect of law.

item.title: Gender Equality Amendment (GEA)
item.dc:creator: allenacnguyen
item.content:encoded:
I, Allen Nguyen — an independent citizen from Houston, TX, and a Summa Cum Laude graduate from the University of Houston with a Bachelor of Science in Digital Media degree — introduce a constitutional amendment that prevent discrimination and denial of rights of transgender and cisgender people to participate in any sort of activities, including sports.

Amendment Slogan

"Equal Dignity. Universal Protection. No Exceptions."

Update 7/6/2026: Updated body text font.

Gender Equality Amendment

Section 1: Gender Equal Rights

Section 1. The equality of rights under the Constitution and laws of the United States shall not be denied, abridged, or infringed by the United States or by any State on account of sex or any gender‑related characteristic, including but not limited to gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, cisgender status, sexual characteristics, or any analogous classification.

Section 2: Equal Participation and Economic Opportunity

Section 2. Every person shall have an equal right to participate in all public, civic, educational, occupational, professional, athletic, recreational, governmental, commercial, and social activities, including all places of public accommodation and commercial enterprise, without discrimination on account of characteristics protected by this article.

No employer, labor organization, licensing authority, educational institution, or governmental entity shall deny employment, hiring, promotion, compensation, licensing, professional advancement, workplace benefits, educational opportunities, or economic participation on account of such characteristics. Qualifications for any occupation or opportunity must be directly related to essential functions and applied uniformly without unlawful discrimination.

Section 3: Equal Access and Nondiscrimination

Section 3. No law, regulation, policy, practice, or governmental action shall deny, exclude, segregate, or impose unequal treatment upon any person on account of characteristics protected by this article. Any classification based on such characteristics shall be subject to strict scrutiny, meaning it shall be upheld only if the government demonstrates a compelling interest and proves the measure is narrowly tailored and uses the least restrictive means available.

Section 4: Athletics and Competitive Activities

Section 4. No person shall be categorically excluded from athletics or competitive activities solely on account of characteristics protected by this article. Eligibility standards must be fair, evidence‑based, consistently applied, and nondiscriminatory, relying on demonstrable, peer‑reviewed evidence. No categorical exclusion shall be imposed without an objective, individualized assessment based on empirical, peer-reviewed scientific data, and all standards must be narrowly tailored to a compelling governmental interest using the least restrictive means available while preserving equal protection and due process.

Section 5: Privacy, Dignity, and Equal Protection

Section 5. Every person shall enjoy equal dignity, privacy, and protection under the law regardless of characteristics protected by this article. No governmental entity shall compel or indirectly compel disclosure of a person’s medical history, gender transition status, or other protected personal information except pursuant to due process of law and a compelling governmental interest.

Section 6: Construction

Section 6. Nothing in this article shall be construed to diminish or impair any right guaranteed elsewhere in this Constitution or by laws enacted pursuant thereto. This article shall be interpreted liberally and broadly to secure equal rights, equal opportunity, equal participation, and equal protection for all persons.

Section 7: Enforcement Clause

Section 7. Congress shall have the plenary power to enforce and implement this article by appropriate legislation, including the creation of private rights of action.

States may enact protections greater than those guaranteed herein, but no State or political subdivision may enact or enforce any law that diminishes or infringes the rights secured by this article.

Section 8: Effect Delay Clause

Section 8. This article of amendment shall take effect one year after ratification. During the period preceding its effective date, the United States and the several States may enact legislation and adopt regulations necessary for implementation, provided that no such action may undermine or frustrate the purpose of this article.

The reason why I introduce this constitutional amendment

I believe gender equality should be a constitutional right and should not be discriminated nor denied the right to participate in such activities among transgender and cisgender people. This includes transgender girls (were boys at first) being denied the right to participate in girl-related activities (especially if it's gender-exclusive), including sports.

The purpose of the Gender Equality Amendment (GEA) is to recognize transgender and cisgender people the equal right to participate in such activities and should not be discriminated against.

In this constitutional amendment, I choose not to include the sunset clause, which would give states in the nation a limited amount of time to ratify passed amendments. So, by excluding the sunset clause, I choose to give states flexibility upon passage by Congress on legislative discussions to ratify this constitutional amendment on the explicit mention and importance of insurance.

Constitutional amendments require broad public support and careful national debate. While the Insurance and Financial Security Amendment (IFSA) may be controversial, I welcome constructive comments, criticism, and proposed changes from the public as part of the constitutional process. This is one of my amendment ideas that I believe that transgender and cisgender people should have a right to any such activity.

Steps to take this amendment into law

Once I finalize the draft of this constitutional amendment with some help from other people, legal scholars, or lawmakers by means of review and evaluation, then I would send this amendment article to Washington, D.C., at the U.S. Capitol Hill for Congress to attempt to pass this amendment.

First, under Article V of the United States Constitution in terms of getting the amendment into law, Congress must vote 2/3 in both the House of Representatives and the Senate to pass this constitutional amendment.

  • 290 out of 435 House of Representatives are required to pass
  • 67 out of 100 Senators are required to pass

Alternatively, under Article V of the United States Constitution, a national convention can be called on proposing this constitutional amendment if 2/3 (34 out of 50 states) of state legislatures apply to Congress to do so. This method was never utilized in U.S. history.

Once this constitutional amendment is passed by Congress, then the next step is ratification, which requires at least 3/4 of the states to ratify this constitutional amendment.

  • 38 out of 50 States are required to ratify

If this Gender Equality Amendment (GEA) is ratified into the United States Constitution, then it would become the 28th Amendment to the United States Constitution (or 29th Amendment if the Equal Rights Amendment (ERA) is officially ratified and certified first that it was in legal limbo for decades since expiration). This constitutional amendment would recognize transgender and cisgender people the equality of rights and should not be discriminated against by other people or the government.

item.title: Campaign Finance Integrity Amendment (CFIA)
item.dc:creator: allenacnguyen
item.content:encoded:
I, Allen Nguyen — an independent citizen from Houston, TX, and a Summa Cum Laude graduate from the University of Houston with a Bachelor of Science in Digital Media degree — introduce a constitutional amendment that modern progressive lawmakers seek to overturn Citizens United v. Federal Elections Commission (2010) for fair funding of individual political campaigns in elections, eliminate or restrict Super PACs (Political Action Committees) in terms of setting contribution amount limits in future election campaigns, and eliminate corporate personhood.

Amendment Slogan

"People Over Profits. Voice Over Wealth."

Inspired & Sponsored by: Marialana Kinter (D-FL, Candidate for Congress, FL-07)

From the Draft Room to the Campaign Trail

This proposed constitutional amendment is directly inspired by the legislative ambitions of Marialana Kinter (D-FL), a U.S. Navy veteran and former Nuclear Reactor Plant Supervisor currently running for Congress in Florida’s 7th congressional district.

Having watched her campaign highlights and platform videos advocating for a clean democracy, her fierce commitment to rejecting corporate PAC influence and introducing a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United v. FEC became the blueprint for this text. Applying the same technical rigor required to operate a naval nuclear reactor, this text has been precision-engineered to not only strip corporate personhood from American elections but to completely close modern digital loopholes regarding artificial intelligence (AI) and cryptocurrency evasion.

Update 7/8/2026: Created CFIA article.

Campaign Finance Integrity Amendment

Section 1: Protection of the Rights of Natural Persons

Section 1. The rights protected by this Constitution are the rights of natural persons. Artificial entities — including corporations, limited liability companies, partnerships, labor organizations, nonprofit organizations, political committees, associations, and other entities established by law — shall have only those constitutional rights granted by the people through federal or state law, except for those procedural due process rights necessary to ensure a fair trial, protection against unlawful searches and seizures, or as explicitly granted by federal or state law. No artificial entity shall possess constitutional protections regarding the raising or spending of funds to influence elections.

Section 2: Regulation and Limitations Authority

Section 2. Congress and the States shall have the absolute authority to regulate, limit, and prohibit the raising and spending of money to influence federal, state, and local elections, including activities such as contributions, independent expenditures, coordinated expenditures, electioneering communications, ballot measure campaigns, and other expenditures intended to influence the nomination or election of candidates or the outcome of public ballot measures. Such regulation may provide for prohibiting or regulating foreign financial influence in those elections, and may be exercised to protect the integrity of the electoral process, prevent corruption and the appearance of corruption, prevent circumvention of campaign finance laws, and promote political equality.

Section 3: Disclosure Clause

Section 3. Congress and the States may require timely public disclosure of the true sources, beneficial owners, and amounts of funds used to influence elections, prohibit the concealment or misrepresentation of the true source of such funds, require disclosure of foreign sources of election-related funding as provided by law, and may establish systems of public financing for campaigns.

Section 4: Free Speech Clause

Section 4. Nothing in this article shall be construed to permit Congress or the States to abridge the freedom of speech or of the press, prohibit individuals from expressing political views, or discriminate against speakers or viewpoints based on the content of their expression; provided that the freedom of the press shall not be construed to immunize any artificial entity from regulations enacted pursuant to Section 2 of this article when engaging in electioneering communications. The regulation, limitation, or prohibition of financial contributions and expenditures authorized by Section 2 of this article shall be deemed fully consistent with the freedoms of speech and of the press, and shall not be construed as an abridgment thereof. Regulation authorized by this article shall be viewpoint-neutral.

Section 5: Definitions Clause

Section 5. For purposes of this article, "artificial entity" means any corporation, limited liability company, partnership, association, labor organization, political committee, nonprofit organization, or other legal entity created under the laws of the United States, any State, or any foreign jurisdiction. The terms "money," "funds," and "expenditures" shall explicitly include digital assets, cryptocurrencies, blockchain-based tokens, algorithmic systems, artificial intelligence technologies, or any other form of digital or synthetic value used to influence elections.

Section 6: Anti-Evasion Clause

Section 6. Congress and the several States shall have the authority to prohibit the circumvention or evasion of laws enacted pursuant to this article through intermediaries, affiliated entities, successor entities, coordinated activities, artificial entities, foreign persons or foreign-controlled entities, emerging technologies, decentralized networks, digital asset architectures, artificial intelligence, automated algorithmic campaigns, or any other means intended to defeat the purposes of this article.

Section 7: Enforcement Clause

Section 7. Congress shall have the power to enforce and implement this article by appropriate legislation, and the several States shall retain concurrent authority to enact and enforce laws consistent with this article.

Section 8: Effect Delay Clause

Section 8. This article of amendment shall take effect six months after ratification. During the period preceding its effective date, the United States and the several States may enact legislation and adopt regulations necessary for implementation, provided that no such action may undermine or frustrate the purpose of this article.

📊 The CFIA Portfolio Evaluation Matrix

Summary

While historic amendments were drafted for a paper-money democracy, the CFIA is engineered for a digital-media reality. By explicitly naming AI and blockchain architectures, it ensures that corporate influence cannot simply hide behind a line of code or a decentralized server.

The reason why I introduce this constitutional amendment

I believe Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission (2010) should be overturned with a constitutional amendment that many progressive lawmakers and people want for the purpose of fair funding of political campaigns in elections, including the elimination or restriction of Super PACs (Political Action Committees). I also believe that elections can't be bought, even by some of the richest people (including Elon Musk).

The purpose of the Campaign Finance Integrity Amendment (CFIA) is to resolve campaign finance issues in regards to the controversial Citizens United v. FEC landmark decision, and resolve contribution limits in political campaigns.

In this constitutional amendment, I choose not to include the sunset clause, which would give states in the nation a limited amount of time to ratify passed amendments. So, by excluding the sunset clause, I choose to give states flexibility upon passage by Congress on legislative discussions to ratify this constitutional amendment on the overturning of Citizens United v. FEC for fair funding of political campaigns in elections.

Constitutional amendments require broad public support and careful national debate. While the Campaign Finance Integrity Amendment (CFIA) may be controversial, I welcome constructive comments, criticism, and proposed changes from the public as part of the constitutional process. This is the amendment idea that I take and study from congressional candidate Marialana Kinter (D-FL), and progressive lawmakers (i.e. Sen. Bernie Sanders [I-VT], Rep. Summer Lee [D-PA], Rep. Alexandria-Ocasio Cortez [D-NY], Rep. Pramila Jayapal [D-WA], and Rep. Rashida Tlaib [D-MI]) that they hope to overturn Citizens United v. FEC (2010), eliminate or restrict Super PACs, and potentially impose contribution amount limits in election campaign funding.

Steps to take this amendment into law

Once I finalize the draft of this constitutional amendment with some help from other people, legal scholars, or lawmakers by means of review and evaluation, then I would send this amendment article to Washington, D.C., at the U.S. Capitol Hill for Congress to attempt to pass this amendment.

First, under Article V of the United States Constitution in terms of getting the amendment into law, Congress must vote 2/3 in both the House of Representatives and the Senate to pass this constitutional amendment.

  • 290 out of 435 House of Representatives are required to pass
  • 67 out of 100 Senators are required to pass

Alternatively, under Article V of the United States Constitution, a national convention can be called on proposing this constitutional amendment if 2/3 (34 out of 50 states) of state legislatures apply to Congress to do so. This method was never utilized in U.S. history.

Once this constitutional amendment is passed by Congress, then the next step is ratification, which requires at least 3/4 of the states to ratify this constitutional amendment.

  • 38 out of 50 States are required to ratify

If this Campaign Finance Integrity Amendment (CFIA) is ratified into the United States Constitution, then it would become the 28th Amendment to the United States Constitution (or 29th Amendment if the Equal Rights Amendment (ERA) is officially ratified and certified first that it was in legal limbo for decades since expiration).

Sponsorship List

  • Rep. Pramila Jayapal (D-WA) — Introduced the "We the People Amendment"
  • Rep.-candidate Marialana Kinter (D-FL) — Congressional Candidate for FL-07. She prioritizes amendment proposal to overturn Citizens United if she were a member of Congress on her first day.
  • Rep. Summer Lee (D-PA) — Co-introduced "Abolish Super PACs Act" with Sen. Sanders
  • Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) — Championed Rep. Jayapal's "We the People Amendment;" seeks to overturn Citizens United
  • Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) — Co-introduced "Abolish Super PACs Act" with Rep. Lee; critic against Citizens United
  • Rep. Rashida Tlaib (D-MI) — Co-sponsored the "Democracy for All Amendment"

NOTE: If you want me to credit you on this list on this constitutional amendment article, then leave a comment on this article that you are supporting this amendment on overturning of Citizens United and eliminating corporate personhood.
